ततो ब्रह्मा सुरैः सर्वैः संमन्त्र्य नृपसत्तम ॥
2.36.m: and the oceans are pervaded by large fish and others; therefore, there is no untouchable place in these." / Then Brahmā, having deliberated with all the gods, O best of kings,

2.36.s:
uvāca mohinīṃ devīṃ nāsti sthānaṃ tava kvacit /
tacchrutvā mohinī vākyaṃ piturājñāvidhāyinī //
2.36.d:
उवाच मोहिनीं देवीं नास्ति स्थानं तव क्वचित् ।
तच्छ्रुत्वा मोहिनी वाक्यं पितुराज्ञाविधायिनी ॥
2.36.m: spoke to goddess Mohinī: "There is no place for you anywhere." / Hearing that speech, Mohinī, obedient to her father's command,

2.36.s:
uvāca praṇatā sarvān harivāsaranāśinī /
purodhasā sametāno devānāṃ lokasākṣiṇām //
2.36.d:
उवाच प्रणता सर्वान् हरिवासरनाशिनी ।
पुरोधसा समेतानो देवानां लोकसाक्षिणाम् ॥
2.36.m: bowed down and spoke to all the gods, the witnesses of the worlds, accompanied by their priest, / she who had destroyed the day of Hari:

2.36.s:
bhavatāṃ tridaśaśreṣṭhā eṣa baddho mayāñjaliḥ /
praṇipātaśatenāpi prasannena hṛdā surāḥ //
2.36.d:
भवतां त्रिदशश्रेष्ठा एष बद्धो मयाञ्जलिः ।
प्रणिपातशतेनापि प्रसन्नेन हृदा सुराः ॥
2.36.m: "O best of the thirty [gods], my hands are joined in reverence to you. / Even with a hundred prostrations, O gods, with a gracious heart,

2.36.s:
dātavyaṃ yācitaṃ maṃhyaṃ sarveṣāṃ prītikārakam /
ekādaśyāḥ prabhāveṇa sarveṣāṃ pāpināṃ gatiḥ //
2.36.d:
दातव्यं याचितं मंह्यं सर्वेषां प्रीतिकारकम् ।
एकादश्याः प्रभावेण सर्वेषां पापिनां गतिः ॥
2.36.m: what is begged by me, which brings pleasure to all, should be granted: / by the power of the ekādaśī, the salvation of all sinners

2.36.s:
sādhyate tāṃ suraśreṣṭhā vardhituṃ me prayojanam /
patiḥ sapatnī putraśca mayā vaikuṇṭhagāḥ kṛtāḥ //
2.36.d:
साध्यते तां सुरश्रेष्ठा वर्धितुं मे प्रयोजनम् ।
पतिः सपत्नी पुत्रश्च मया वैकुण्ठगाः कृताः ॥
2.36.m: is accomplished; my purpose, O best of gods, is to increase that [sin]. / My husband, co-wife, and son were sent to Vaikuṇṭha by me,

2.36.s:
bhūrloke vidhavādyāhaṃ vartāmi bhavatāṃ kṛte /
yathā haridinaṃ duṣṭaṃ jāyate mama mānadāḥ //
2.36.d:
भूर्लोके विधवाद्याहं वर्तामि भवतां कृते ।
यथा हरिदिनं दुष्टं जायते मम मानदाः ॥
2.36.m: and on the mortal earth I remain today a widow for your sake. / O givers of honor, so that the day of Hari may become corrupted for me,

2.36.s:
etatprayāce dadata svārthārthaṃ taddhi nānyathā //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇottarabhāge mohinīcarite ṣaṭtriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.36.d:
एतत्प्रयाचे ददत स्वार्थार्थं तद्धि नान्यथा ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणोत्तरभागे मोहिनीचरिते षट्त्रिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
2.36.m:
I beg this: grant it for your own purpose, for that is not otherwise."

Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter in the Uttarabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa, in the story of Mohinī.

2.37.s:
mohinyuvāca
ekādaśīsamaṃ devāḥ pāvanaṃ nāparaṃ bhavet /
yayā pūtā mahāpāpā gacchanti harimandiram //
2.37.d:
मोहिन्युवाच
एकादशीसमं देवाः पावनं नापरं भवेत् ।
यया पूता महापापा गच्छन्ति हरिमन्दिरम् ॥
2.37.m: Mohinī said: / "O gods, there can be no purifier equal to the Ekādaśī, / purified by which even great sinners go to the abode of Hari.

2.37.s:
tatsamīpe mama sthānaṃ yuktaṃ bhāti vicāryatām /
devā ūcuḥ
vedho niśīthe devānāmupakārāya mohinī //
2.37.d:
तत्समीपे मम स्थानं युक्तं भाति विचार्यताम् ।
देवा ऊचुः
वेधो निशीथे देवानामुपकाराय मोहिनी ॥
2.37.m: "A place near that seems fitting for me; let it be considered." / The gods said: / "O Brahmā, for the benefit of the gods at midnight, Mohinī [was created].

2.37.s:
sūryodaye surāṇāṃ ca hariṇā parikalpitaḥ /
pāraṇaṃ ca trayodaśyāmupavāsavināśanam //
2.37.d:
सूर्योदये सुराणां च हरिणा परिकल्पितः ।
पारणं च त्रयोदश्यामुपवासविनाशनम् ॥
2.37.m: And at sunrise for the gods, it was ordained by Hari; / and breaking the fast on the thirteenth day destroys the fast.

2.37.s:
mahādvādaśikā hyaṣṭau yāḥ smṛtā vaiṣṇavāgame /
tāstu hyekādaśībhinnā upoṣyante ca vaiṣṇavaiḥ //
2.37.d:
महाद्वादशिका ह्यष्टौ याः स्मृता वैष्णवागमे ।
तास्तु ह्येकादशीभिन्ना उपोष्यन्ते च वैष्णवैः ॥
2.37.m: Indeed, the eight Mahādvādaśīs that are taught in the Vaiṣṇava scripture, / these are separate from the ekādaśī and are fasted upon by Vaiṣṇavas.

2.37.s:
ekādaśīvrataṃ bhinnaṃ vaiṣṇavānāṃ mahātmanām /
nityaṃ pakṣadvaye proktaṃ vidhinā tridinātmake //
2.37.d:
एकादशीव्रतं भिन्नं वैष्णवानां महात्मनाम् ।
नित्यं पक्षद्वये प्रोक्तं विधिना त्रिदिनात्मके ॥
2.37.m: The fast of ekādaśī is separate for the great-souled Vaiṣṇavas; / it is declared as a regular duty in both fortnights, according to the rule of a three-day period.

2.37.s:
sāyaṃ prātastyajedbhuktiṃ kramātpūrvāparāhṇayoḥ /
ekādaśī yadā bhinnā upoṣyā hi pare 'hani /
dvādaśyāṃ hi vrataṃ kāryaṃ niraṃbu samupoṣaṇam //
2.37.d:
सायं प्रातस्त्यजेद्भुक्तिं क्रमात्पूर्वापराह्णयोः ।
एकादशी यदा भिन्ना उपोष्या हि परे ऽहनि ।
द्वादश्यां हि व्रतं कार्यं निरंबु समुपोषणम् ॥
2.37.m: One should give up food in the evening and morning, successively, in the forenoon and afternoon; / when the ekādaśī is broken, the fast must be observed on the next day; / indeed, on the twelfth day, the fast should be undertaken without water.

2.37.s:
laṅghane tvasamarthānāṃ jalaṃ śākaṃ phalaṃ payaḥ /
naivedyaṃ vā hareḥ proktaṃ svāhārātpādasaṃmitam //
2.37.d:
लङ्घने त्वसमर्थानां जलं शाकं फलं पयः ।
नैवेद्यं वा हरेः प्रोक्तं स्वाहारात्पादसंमितम् ॥
2.37.m: For those unable to fast completely: water, herbs, fruit, milk, / or Hari's food-offering is prescribed, measured as a fourth part of one's usual meal.

2.37.s:
svātī sūryodaye viddho tyajantyakādaśīṃ sati /
niṣkāmā madhyarātre ca viddhāṃ muñcanti yāmyayā //
2.37.d:
स्वाती सूर्योदये विद्धो त्यजन्त्यकादशीं सति ।
निष्कामा मध्यरात्रे च विद्धां मुञ्चन्ति याम्यया ॥
2.37.m: When it is pierced at sunrise by the constellation Svātī, O virtuous lady, they abandon the ekādaśī; / and those free from desire abandon it when it is pierced at midnight by the constellation of Yama.

2.37.s:
sarveṣvapi tu lokeṣu viditā daśamī tithiḥ /
yamasya tasyāḥ prānti tu sthitiḥ kāryā tvayānaghe //
2.37.d:
सर्वेष्वपि तु लोकेषु विदिता दशमी तिथिः ।
यमस्य तस्याः प्रान्ति तु स्थितिः कार्या त्वयानघे ॥
2.37.m: The tenth lunar day is known in all worlds / as belonging to Yama; at its end, O sinless one, your stay is to be made.

2.37.s:
etena devakāryaṃ ca siddhaṃ bhavati śobhane /
sūryenducārā tithyāstu daśamyāḥ prāntagāminī //
2.37.d:
एतेन देवकार्यं च सिद्धं भवति शोभने ।
सूर्येन्दुचारा तिथ्यास्तु दशम्याः प्रान्तगामिनी ॥
2.37.m: By this, the work of the gods will also be accomplished, O lovely one. / Following the course of the sun and moon, it goes to the end of the tenth lunar day.

2.37.s:
bhuvi tīrthāni caiva tvaṃ svāghanāśāya saṃcara /
aruṇodayamārabhya yāvatsūryodayo bhavet //
2.37.d:
भुवि तीर्थानि चैव त्वं स्वाघनाशाय संचर ।
अरुणोदयमारभ्य यावत्सूर्योदयो भवेत् ॥
2.37.m: Roam about the sacred fords on earth for the destruction of your own sin, / starting from dawn until sunrise takes place.

2.37.s:
tadantastvaṃ vrate prāptā labhasvaikādaśīphalam /
yaḥ kaścitkurute viddhaṃ tvayā hyekādaśīvratam //
2.37.d:
तदन्तस्त्वं व्रते प्राप्ता लभस्वैकादशीफलम् ।
यः कश्चित्कुरुते विद्धं त्वया ह्येकादशीव्रतम् ॥
2.37.m: Entering into the observance within that [interval], obtain the fruit of ekādaśī. / Whosoever undertakes the fast of ekādaśī pierced by you,

2.37.s:
sa tīpakārakastubhyaṃ bhaviṣyati surapriye /
muhūrtadvayamātraṃ tu jñeyaṃ cātrāruṇodayam //
2.37.d:
स तीपकारकस्तुभ्यं भविष्यति सुरप्रिये ।
मुहूर्तद्वयमात्रं तु ज्ञेयं चात्रारुणोदयम् ॥
2.37.m: he will be a benefactor to you, O beloved of the gods! / The dawn here is to be understood as measuring just two muhūrtas.

2.37.s:
mūhūrtāḥ pañcadaśa ca smṛtā rātrerdinasya ca /
jñeyāste hrasvadīrghatve trairāśika vidhānataḥ //
2.37.d:
मूहूर्ताः पञ्चदश च स्मृता रात्रेर्दिनस्य च ।
ज्ञेयास्ते ह्रस्वदीर्घत्वे त्रैराशिक विधानतः ॥
2.37.m: Fifteen muhūrtas are remembered for the night and for the day; / they should be known in their shortness or length by the method of the rule of three.

2.37.s:
trayodaśānmuhūrtānttu rātrairūrddhvā samāgatā /
sabdhvopavāsināṃ puṇyaṃ svasthā bhava śucismite //
2.37.d:
त्रयोदशान्मुहूर्तान्त्तु रात्रैरूर्द्ध्वा समागता ।
सब्ध्वोपवासिनां पुण्यं स्वस्था भव शुचिस्मिते ॥
2.37.m: Having arrived beyond the thirteenth muhūrta of the night, / obtain the merit of those who fast, and be at ease, O sweet-smiling one!

2.37.s:
yamasaṃsthāpanārthāya vaikuṇṭhadhvaṃsanāya ca /
pākhaṇḍānāṃ vivṛddhyarthaṃ pāpasaṃcanāya ca //
2.37.d:
यमसंस्थापनार्थाय वैकुण्ठध्वंसनाय च ।
पाखण्डानां विवृद्ध्यर्थं पापसंचनाय च ॥
2.37.m: For the purpose of establishing Yama, for the destruction of Vaikuṇṭha, / for the increase of heretics, and for the accumulation of sins,

2.37.s: dattaṃ te mohini sthānaṃ pratyūṣasamayāṅkitam //
2.37.d: दत्तं ते मोहिनि स्थानं प्रत्यूषसमयाङ्कितम् ॥
2.37.m: a place marked by the time of dawn has been given to you, O Mohinī!

2.37.s:
viddhaṃ tvayaikādaśikāvrataṃ ye kurvanti kartāra iha prayatnāt /
teṣāṃ bhavedyatsukṛtaṃ śubhe phalaṃ bhuṅkṣva prasannā bhava bhūsure tvam //
2.37.d:
विद्धं त्वयैकादशिकाव्रतं ये कुर्वन्ति कर्तार इह प्रयत्नात् ।
तेषां भवेद्यत्सुकृतं शुभे फलं भुङ्क्ष्व प्रसन्ना भव भूसुरे त्वम् ॥
2.37.m: Whatever merit and auspicious fruit belongs to those who observe here with effort / the vow of ekādaśī pierced by you, enjoy that, O auspicious one, and be gracious to the brāhmaṇa!"

2.37.s:
evaṃ pradiṣṭā kamalāsanādyaiḥ sā mohinī hṛṣṭatarā babhūva /
mene kṛtārthaṃ nijajīvitaṃ ca svapāpatīrthābhiniṣevaṇena //
2.37.d:
एवं प्रदिष्टा कमलासनाद्यैः सा मोहिनी हृष्टतरा बभूव ।
मेने कृतार्थं निजजीवितं च स्वपापतीर्थाभिनिषेवणेन ॥
2.37.m: Directed thus by the lotus-seated Brahmā and others, that Mohinī became overjoyed, / and she considered her life fulfilled by attending to her sacred ford of sin.

2.37.s:
saṃsādhitaṃ kāryamidaṃ surāṇāṃ bhasmāvaśeṣaṃ hi gate 'pi dehe /
caitanyamātre pavanātmake 'smin saṃmārjito bhūpakṛtastu panthāḥ //
2.37.d:
संसाधितं कार्यमिदं सुराणां भस्मावशेषं हि गते ऽपि देहे ।
चैतन्यमात्रे पवनात्मके ऽस्मिन् संमार्जितो भूपकृतस्तु पन्थाः ॥
2.37.m: "This task of the gods has been accomplished, even though my body has been reduced to ashes; / in this mere consciousness of the nature of wind, the path made by the king has been wiped away.

2.37.s:
nītaṃ mayā cātmakṛtaṃ hi vākyaṃ prahṛṣṭayā vai yadudāhṛtaṃ hi /
evaṃ vimṛśya kṣiptipālade vānpraṇamya hṛṣṭā ca purodhasaṃ svam //
2.37.d:
नीतं मया चात्मकृतं हि वाक्यं प्रहृष्टया वै यदुदाहृतं हि ।
एवं विमृश्य क्षिप्तिपालदे वान्प्रणम्य हृष्टा च पुरोधसं स्वम् ॥
2.37.m: And I have brought about my own promise that was uttered when overjoyed." / Reflecting thus, having bowed to the kings, the gods, and her own priest, overjoyed,

2.37.s:
prānte sthitā sūryavihīnasaṃjñe kāle daśamyā janamohanāya /
kṛcchrāntarūpā ca dinaṃ ca bhuṅkte prakṛṣṭarūpā narakāya nṝṇām //
2.37.d:
प्रान्ते स्थिता सूर्यविहीनसंज्ञे काले दशम्या जनमोहनाय ।
कृच्छ्रान्तरूपा च दिनं च भुङ्क्ते प्रकृष्टरूपा नरकाय नॄणाम् ॥
2.37.m: she stood at the end [of the tenth day], at the time known as devoid of sun, to delude people; / assuming the form of an ordeal, she consumes the day, appearing in an extraordinary form, for the hell of men.

2.37.s:
prāntasthitāṃ tāṃ ravijo nirīkṣya prahṛṣṭavaktro vacanaṃ jagāda /
tvayā pratiṣṭhā mama cārunetre kṛtātra loke punareva samyak /
vibhodito rukmavibhūṣaṇasya mattebhasaṃsthaḥ paṭahaḥ sughaiṣaḥ //
2.37.d:
प्रान्तस्थितां तां रविजो निरीक्ष्य प्रहृष्टवक्त्रो वचनं जगाद ।
त्वया प्रतिष्ठा मम चारुनेत्रे कृतात्र लोके पुनरेव सम्यक् ।
विभोदितो रुक्मविभूषणस्य मत्तेभसंस्थः पटहः सुघैषः ॥
2.37.m: Seeing her standing at the end, the son of the Sun [Yama], with a joyful face, spoke these words: / "By you, O fair-eyed one, my standing has been properly re-established in this world; / the loud-sounding drum of Rukmāṅgada, seated on a rutted elephant, has been silenced.

2.37.s: dṛṣṭe kārye janaḥ sarvaḥ pratyayaṃ kurute tviti //
2.37.d: दृष्टे कार्ये जनः सर्वः प्रत्ययं कुरुते त्विति ॥
2.37.m: For when a deed is seen, all people place their trust in it."

2.37.s:
sūryodaya spṛṣā hyeṣā daśamī garhitā sadā /
aspṛṣṭamudayaṃ nṝṇāṃ mohanāya bhaviṣyati //
2.37.d:
सूर्योदय स्पृषा ह्येषा दशमी गर्हिता सदा ।
अस्पृष्टमुदयं नॄणां मोहनाय भविष्यति ॥
2.37.m: For this tenth day, when touching sunrise, is ever reviled; / untouched by sunrise, it shall serve to delude mankind.

2.37.s:
vihāya tāṃ yatpriyayogabhuktiṃ pādasthitā sāpi hyadṛṣyarūpā /
satyaṃ hi te nāma viśālanetre yanmohinītyeva jano bravīti //
2.37.d:
विहाय तां यत्प्रिययोगभुक्तिं पादस्थिता सापि ह्यदृष्यरूपा ।
सत्यं हि ते नाम विशालनेत्रे यन्मोहिनीत्येव जनो ब्रवीति ॥
2.37.m: Leaving aside the enjoyment of union with her beloved, she stood at his feet, invisible in form. / Truly, O large-eyed woman, your name is fitting, since people call you Mohinī.

2.37.s:
vimohayitvā hi janaṃ samastaṃ paṭe madīye likhitaṃ karoṣi /
ityeva muktvā tanayo vivasvataḥ praṇamya tāṃ brahmasutāṃ prahṛṣṭaḥ //
2.37.d:
विमोहयित्वा हि जनं समस्तं पटे मदीये लिखितं करोषि ।
इत्येव मुक्त्वा तनयो विवस्वतः प्रणम्य तां ब्रह्मसुतां प्रहृष्टः ॥
2.37.m: Having thoroughly deluded all people, you cause them to be recorded on my scroll.” / Having spoken thus, the son of Vivasvat bowed to that daughter of Brahmā, delighted,

2.37.s:
jagāma devaiḥ saha nākalokaṃ kare gṛhītvā lipilekhitāram /
gateṣu deveṣu vimohinī sā brahmāṇamāsādya surāsureśam //
2.37.d:
जगाम देवैः सह नाकलोकं करे गृहीत्वा लिपिलेखितारम् ।
गतेषु देवेषु विमोहिनी सा ब्रह्माणमासाद्य सुरासुरेशम् ॥
2.37.m: and went with the gods to the celestial world, taking by the hand his scribe of records. / When the gods had gone, that enchanting Mohinī approached Brahmā, the lord of gods and asuras,

2.37.s:
vijñāpayāmāsa pitaḥ purodhā mamāyamatyugrataraśca kopāt /
dagdhaṃ śarīraṃ mama lokanātha punaḥ prapatsye 'tha tathā kuruṣva //
2.37.d:
विज्ञापयामास पितः पुरोधा ममायमत्युग्रतरश्च कोपात् ।
दग्धं शरीरं मम लोकनाथ पुनः प्रपत्स्ये ऽथ तथा कुरुष्व ॥
2.37.m: and made a petition: “O Father, this family priest of mine, through extreme anger, / has burnt my body, O lord of the world! Make it so that I may attain it once again.

2.37.s:
vimohitaṃ caiva jaganmayedaṃ prānte samāsthāya yamasya tithyāḥ /
jito hi rājñā śamanaḥ purādya kṛto jayī tāta tava prabhāvāt //
2.37.d:
विमोहितं चैव जगन्मयेदं प्रान्ते समास्थाय यमस्य तिथ्याः ।
जितो हि राज्ञा शमनः पुराद्य कृतो जयी तात तव प्रभावात् ॥
2.37.m: Indeed, this world was deluded by me, abiding at the end of the tithi of Yama. / Formerly Śamana was defeated by the king, but today, O father, he has been made victorious through your power.

2.37.s:
tava kṛtyamidaṃ tāta yatpunardehadhāriṇī /
bhūyāmahaṃ jagannātha brahmaṇaṃ sāṃtyayasva bhoḥ //
2.37.d:
तव कृत्यमिदं तात यत्पुनर्देहधारिणी ।
भूयामहं जगन्नाथ ब्रह्मणं सांत्ययस्व भोः ॥
2.37.m: This is your task, O father, that I should once more become endowed with a body. / O lord of the world, please conciliate the brāhmaṇa!”

2.37.s:
tacchrutvā mohinīvākyaṃ brahmā lokavidhānakṛt /
brāhmaṇaṃ sāṃtvayāmāsa punareva sutākṛte //
2.37.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा मोहिनीवाक्यं ब्रह्मा लोकविधानकृत् ।
ब्राह्मणं सांत्वयामास पुनरेव सुताकृते ॥
2.37.m: Hearing that speech of Mohinī, Brahmā, the ordainer of the worlds, / conciliated the brāhmaṇa once more for the sake of his daughter:

2.37.s:
vaso tāta nibodhedaṃ yadbravīmi hitāvaham /
tava cāsyā mahābhāga sarvalokahitāya ca //
2.37.d:
वसो तात निबोधेदं यद्ब्रवीमि हितावहम् ।
तव चास्या महाभाग सर्वलोकहिताय च ॥
2.37.m: “O dear Vasu, listen to this beneficial word which I speak / for your sake and hers, O highly fortunate one, and for the welfare of all worlds.

2.37.s:
tvayeyaṃ mohinī kopātkṛtā bhasmāvaśeṣitā /
punaḥ śarīraṃ yāceta tadājñāṃ dehi mānada //
2.37.d:
त्वयेयं मोहिनी कोपात्कृता भस्मावशेषिता ।
पुनः शरीरं याचेत तदाज्ञां देहि मानद ॥
2.37.m: Out of anger, this Mohinī was reduced by you to mere ashes. / She begs for a body again; therefore give your permission, O giver of honor.

2.37.s:
matputrī tava yājyeyaṃ durgatiṃ tāta gacchati /
tvayā mayā ca sapālyā kṛtakāryā tapasvinī //
2.37.d:
मत्पुत्री तव याज्येयं दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति ।
त्वया मया च सपाल्या कृतकार्या तपस्विनी ॥
2.37.m: This daughter of mine, your patroness, is going to an evil state, dear one. / She, a performer of austerities, must be protected by both you and me, having accomplished her purpose.

2.37.s:
yadi tvaṃ śuddhabhāvena māṃ jñāpayasi mānada /
tāto 'hamasyā bhūyo 'pi dehamutpādayāmyaham //
2.37.d:
यदि त्वं शुद्धभावेन मां ज्ञापयसि मानद ।
तातो ऽहमस्या भूयो ऽपि देहमुत्पादयाम्यहम् ॥
2.37.m: If you direct me with a pure disposition, O giver of honor, / then I, her father, shall once again produce her body.

2.37.s:
kintu viṣṇudinasyaiṣā vairiṇī pāpakāriṇī /
yathā śuddhyeti viprendra tathaivāśu vidhīyatām //
2.37.d:
किन्तु विष्णुदिनस्यैषा वैरिणी पापकारिणी ।
यथा शुद्ध्येति विप्रेन्द्र तथैवाशु विधीयताम् ॥
2.37.m: However, this sinful woman is an enemy of the day of Viṣṇu. / Let it be arranged swiftly, O best of vipras, so that she may be purified.”

2.37.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya brahmaṇaḥ sa purohitaḥ /
yājyāyā dehayogārthamādideśa mudānvitaḥ //
2.37.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य ब्रह्मणः स पुरोहितः ।
याज्याया देहयोगार्थमादिदेश मुदान्वितः ॥
2.37.m: Hearing that speech of Brahmā, that family priest, / filled with joy, gave his command for the bodily restoration of his patroness.

2.37.s:
vipravākyaṃ samākarṇya brahmā lokapitamahaḥ /
kamaṇḍalujalenaukṣanmohinyā dehabhasma tat //
2.37.d:
विप्रवाक्यं समाकर्ण्य ब्रह्मा लोकपितमहः ।
कमण्डलुजलेनौक्षन्मोहिन्या देहभस्म तत् ॥
2.37.m: Hearing the speech of the vipra, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, / sprinkled the ashes of Mohinī’s body with water from his water-pot.

2.37.s:
samukṣite brahmaṇā lokakartrā sā mohinī dehayutā babhūva /
praṇamya tātaṃ ca vasoḥ purodhaso jagrāha pādau vinayena natvā //
2.37.d:
समुक्षिते ब्रह्मणा लोककर्त्रा सा मोहिनी देहयुता बभूव ।
प्रणम्य तातं च वसोः पुरोधसो जग्राह पादौ विनयेन नत्वा ॥
2.37.m: When it was sprinkled by Brahmā, the creator of the worlds, that Mohinī became endowed with a body. / Having bowed to her father and bowing in humility, she touched the feet of the family priest Vasu.

2.37.s:
tato vasuryājaka eva rājño mudānvito yājyanitaṃbinīṃ tām /
vimohinīṃ svāmisutoñjjhitāṃ ca jagāda vākyaṃ vidutāmavīrām //
2.37.d:
ततो वसुर्याजक एव राज्ञो मुदान्वितो याज्यनितंबिनीं ताम् ।
विमोहिनीं स्वामिसुतोञ्ज्झितां च जगाद वाक्यं विदुतामवीराम् ॥
2.37.m: Then Vasu, the sacrificial priest of the king, filled with joy, / spoke words to that wide-hipped patroness, the enchanting woman abandoned by her husband’s son, distressed and husbandless:

2.37.s:
vasuruvāca
krodhastyakto mayā devi brahmaṇo vacanādatha /
gatiṃ te kārayiṣyāmi tīrthasnānādikarmaṇā //
2.37.d:
वसुरुवाच
क्रोधस्त्यक्तो मया देवि ब्रह्मणो वचनादथ ।
गतिं ते कारयिष्यामि तीर्थस्नानादिकर्मणा ॥
2.37.m:
Vasu said:
“O goddess, my anger has now been abandoned at the word of Brahmā. / I shall bring about your good destiny through rites such as bathing in sacred fords.”

2.37.s:
ityuktvā mohinīṃ vipro brahmāṇāṃ jagatāṃ patim /
visasarja namaskṛtya mohinīpitaraṃ mudā //
2.37.d:
इत्युक्त्वा मोहिनीं विप्रो ब्रह्माणां जगतां पतिम् ।
विससर्ज नमस्कृत्य मोहिनीपितरं मुदा ॥
2.37.m: Having spoken thus to Mohinī, the vipra, having bowed, / gladly sent off Brahmā, the lord of the worlds and father of Mohinī.

2.37.s:
mohinyā vasunā caiva prītyā brahmā visarjitaḥ /
jagāma lokaṃ tamasaḥ paramavyaktavartmanā //
2.37.d:
मोहिन्या वसुना चैव प्रीत्या ब्रह्मा विसर्जितः ।
जगाम लोकं तमसः परमव्यक्तवर्त्मना ॥
2.37.m: Brahmā, sent off with affection by both Mohinī and Vasu, / went to the world beyond darkness by the unmanifest path.

2.37.s:
sa vasurbrāhmaṇaśreṣṭho rukmāṅgadapurohitaḥ /
mohinīṃ samanugrāhyāṃ matvā hṛdi vicārayan //
2.37.d:
स वसुर्ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठो रुक्माङ्गदपुरोहितः ।
मोहिनीं समनुग्राह्यां मत्वा हृदि विचारयन् ॥
2.37.m: That Vasu, the best of brāhmaṇas and family priest of Rukmāṅgada, / thinking in his heart that Mohinī was worthy of grace,

2.37.s:
muhūrttaṃ dhyānamāpanno bubudhe kāraṇaṃ gateḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇottarabhāge mohinīcarite saptatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.37.d:
मुहूर्त्तं ध्यानमापन्नो बुबुधे कारणं गतेः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणोत्तरभागे मोहिनीचरिते सप्तत्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
2.37.m:
entered into meditation for a moment and understood the cause of her deliverance.

Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter in the second part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa, on the conduct of Mohinī.

2.38.s:
vasiṣṭaṃ uvāca
sa vasurnṛpaśārdūla mohinīṃ yājyakāminīm /
uvāca ślakṣṇayā vācā sarvalokahite rataḥ //
2.38.d:
वसिष्टं उवाच
स वसुर्नृपशार्दूल मोहिनीं याज्यकामिनीम् ।
उवाच श्लक्ष्णया वाचा सर्वलोकहिते रतः ॥
2.38.m:
Vasiṣṭha said:
O tiger among kings, that Vasu, devoted to the welfare of all worlds, / spoke in gentle words to Mohinī, the passionate woman who was his patroness.

2.38.s:
vasuruvāca
śṛṇu mohinī vakṣyāmi tīrthānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ pṛthak /
yena vijñātamātreṇa pāpināṃ gatiruttamā //
2.38.d:
वसुरुवाच
शृणु मोहिनी वक्ष्यामि तीर्थानां लक्षणं पृथक् ।
येन विज्ञातमात्रेण पापिनां गतिरुत्तमा ॥
2.38.m:
Vasu said:
“Listen, Mohinī, I shall explain the specific characteristics of sacred fords, / merely by knowing which sinners obtain the highest destiny.

2.38.s:
sarveṣāmapi tīrthānāṃ śreṣṭhā gaṃmā dharātale /
na tasyā sadṛśaṃ kiñcidvidyate pāpanāśanam //
2.38.d:
सर्वेषामपि तीर्थानां श्रेष्ठा गंमा धरातले ।
न तस्या सदृशं किञ्चिद्विद्यते पापनाशनम् ॥
2.38.m: Among all sacred fords, the Gaṅgā is the foremost on the surface of the earth; / there exists nothing like her for the destruction of sins.”

2.38.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya vasoḥ svasya purodhasaḥ /
praṇatā mohinī prāha gaṅgāsnānakṛtādarā //
2.38.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य वसोः स्वस्य पुरोधसः ।
प्रणता मोहिनी प्राह गङ्गास्नानकृतादरा ॥
2.38.m: Hearing that speech of Vasu, her family priest, / Mohinī bowed down and, intent on bathing in the Gaṅgā, said:

2.38.s:
mohinyuvāca
bhagavanvāḍavaśreṣṭha gaṅgāmāhātmyamuttamam /
sarveṣāṃ ca purāṇānāṃ saṃmataṃ vada sāṃpratam //
2.38.d:
मोहिन्युवाच
भगवन्वाडवश्रेष्ठ गङ्गामाहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ।
सर्वेषां च पुराणानां संमतं वद सांप्रतम् ॥
2.38.m:
Mohinī said:
“O venerable one, best of brāhmaṇas, tell me now the supreme eulogy of the greatness of the Gaṅgā, / accepted by all the Purāṇas.

2.38.s:
śrutvā māhātmyamatulaṃ gaṅgāyāḥ pāpanāśanam /
paścātpāpavināśinyāṃ snātuṃ yāsye tvayā saha //
2.38.d:
श्रुत्वा माहात्म्यमतुलं गङ्गायाः पापनाशनम् ।
पश्चात्पापविनाशिन्यां स्नातुं यास्ये त्वया सह ॥
2.38.m: Having heard the peerless eulogy of the greatness of the Gaṅgā, which destroys sin, / I shall go afterwards with you to bathe in her who wipes out sin.”

2.38.s:
tacchrutvā mohinīvākyaṃ vasuḥ sarvapurāṇavit /
māhātmyaṃ kathayāmāsa gaṅgāyāḥ pāpanāśanam //
2.38.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा मोहिनीवाक्यं वसुः सर्वपुराणवित् ।
माहात्म्यं कथयामास गङ्गायाः पापनाशनम् ॥
2.38.m: Hearing that speech of Mohinī, Vasu, who knows all Purāṇas, / recounted the eulogy of the greatness of the Gaṅgā that destroys sin.

2.38.s:
vasuruvāca
te deśāste janapadāste śailā ste 'pi cāśramāḥ /
yeṣāṃ bhāgīrathī puṇyā samīpe vartate sadā //
2.38.d:
वसुरुवाच
ते देशास्ते जनपदास्ते शैला स्ते ऽपि चाश्रमाः ।
येषां भागीरथी पुण्या समीपे वर्तते सदा ॥
2.38.m:
Vasu said:
“Those are the [true] lands, those the regions, those the mountains, and those the hermitages / near which the holy Bhāgīrathī ever flows.

2.38.s:
tapasā brahmacaryeṇa yajñaistyāgena vā punaḥ /
tāṃ gatiṃ na labhejjanturgaṅgāṃ saṃsevya yāṃ labhet //
2.38.d:
तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण यज्ञैस्त्यागेन वा पुनः ।
तां गतिं न लभेज्जन्तुर्गङ्गां संसेव्य यां लभेत् ॥
2.38.m: A creature cannot attain by asceticism, by celibacy, by sacrifices, or by renunciation / that state which he attains by resorting to the Gaṅgā.

2.38.s:
pūrve vayasi pāpāni kṛtvā karmāṇi ye narāḥ /
śeṣe gaṅgāṃ niṣevante te 'pi yānti parāṃ gatim //
2.38.d:
पूर्वे वयसि पापानि कृत्वा कर्माणि ये नराः ।
शेषे गङ्गां निषेवन्ते ते ऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम् ॥
2.38.m: Men who, having committed sinful deeds in early life, / resort to the Gaṅgā in their remaining years, even they reach the supreme destination.

2.38.s:
tiṣṭhedyugasahasraṃ tu pādenaikena yaḥ pumān /
māsamekaṃ tu gaṅgāyāṃ snātastulyaphalāvubhau //
2.38.d:
तिष्ठेद्युगसहस्रं तु पादेनैकेन यः पुमान् ।
मासमेकं तु गङ्गायां स्नातस्तुल्यफलावुभौ ॥
2.38.m: A man who stands on one foot for a thousand yugas, / and one who bathes in the Gaṅgā for a single month—both obtain equal fruit.

2.38.s:
tiṣṭhetārvākchirā yastu yugānāmayutaṃ pumān /
tiṣṭhedyatheṣṭaṃ yaścāpi gaṅgāyāṃ sa viśiṣyate //
2.38.d:
तिष्ठेतार्वाक्छिरा यस्तु युगानामयुतं पुमान् ।
तिष्ठेद्यथेष्टं यश्चापि गङ्गायां स विशिष्यते ॥
2.38.m: A man who stands head-downwards for ten thousand yugas, / and he who stays at the Gaṅgā as he pleases—the latter is distinguished [as superior].

2.38.s:
bhūtānāmiha sarveṣāṃ duḥkhopahatacetasām /
gatimanveṣamāṇānāṃ na gaṅgāsadṛśī gatiḥ //
2.38.d:
भूतानामिह सर्वेषां दुःखोपहतचेतसाम् ।
गतिमन्वेषमाणानां न गङ्गासदृशी गतिः ॥
2.38.m: For all beings in this world whose minds are afflicted with misery / and who are searching for a refuge, there is no refuge equal to the Gaṅgā.

2.38.s:
prakṛṣṭaiḥ pātakair ghoraiḥ pāpinaḥ puruṣādhamān /
prasahya tārayedguṅgā gacchato niraye 'śucau //
2.38.d:
प्रकृष्टैः पातकैर् घोरैः पापिनः पुरुषाधमान् ।
प्रसह्य तारयेद्गुङ्गा गच्छतो निरये ऽशुचौ ॥
2.38.m: The Gaṅgā forcefully rescues vile men, sinners with monstrous and grave transgressions, / who are on their way to an impure hell.

2.38.s:
te samānāstu munibhirnūnaṃ devaiḥ savāsavaiḥ /
ye 'bhigacchanti satataṃ gaṅgāmabhimatāṃ suraiḥ //
2.38.d:
ते समानास्तु मुनिभिर्नूनं देवैः सवासवैः ।
ये ऽभिगच्छन्ति सततं गङ्गामभिमतां सुरैः ॥
2.38.m: Those who constantly approach the Gaṅgā, who is beloved by the gods, / are truly equal to the sages and to the gods together with Indra.

2.38.s:
andhāñjaḍāndravyahīnāṃśca gaṅgā saṃpāvayedbṛhatī viśvarūpā /
devaiḥ seṃdrairmunibhirmānavaiśca niṣevitā sarvakālaṃ samṛddhye //
2.38.d:
अन्धाञ्जडान्द्रव्यहीनांश्च गङ्गा संपावयेद्बृहती विश्वरूपा ।
देवैः सेंद्रैर्मुनिभिर्मानवैश्च निषेविता सर्वकालं समृद्ध्ये ॥
2.38.m: The vast, all-formed Gaṅgā purifies the blind, the dull-witted, and those destitute of wealth; / she is attended by the gods along with Indra, by sages, and by men at all times for prosperity.

2.38.s:
pakṣādau kṛṣṇapakṣe tu bhūmau saṃnihitā bhavet /
yāvatpuṇyā hyamāvāsyā dināni daśa mohini //
2.38.d:
पक्षादौ कृष्णपक्षे तु भूमौ संनिहिता भवेत् ।
यावत्पुण्या ह्यमावास्या दिनानि दश मोहिनि ॥
2.38.m: At the beginning of the fortnight, in the dark fortnight, she is present on earth / until the holy new-moon day, for ten days, O Mohinī.

2.38.s:
śuklapratipadādeśca dināni daśa saṃkhyayā /
pātāle sannidhānaṃ tu kurute svayameva hi //
2.38.d:
शुक्लप्रतिपदादेश्च दिनानि दश संख्यया ।
पाताले सन्निधानं तु कुरुते स्वयमेव हि ॥
2.38.m: From the first day of the bright fortnight, for the number of ten days, / she personally establishes her presence in the netherworld.

2.38.s:
ārabhya śuklaikādaśyā dināni daśa yāni tu /
pañcamyaṃ tāni sā svarge bhavetsannihitā sadā //
2.38.d:
आरभ्य शुक्लैकादश्या दिनानि दश यानि तु ।
पञ्चम्यं तानि सा स्वर्गे भवेत्सन्निहिता सदा ॥
2.38.m: Beginning from the eleventh day of the bright fortnight, for those ten days / ending with the fifth [of the dark fortnight], she is ever present in heaven.

2.38.s:
kṛte tu sarvatīrthāni tretāyāṃ puṣkaraṃ param /
dvāpare tu kurukṣetraṃ kalau gaṅgā viśiṣyate //
2.38.d:
कृते तु सर्वतीर्थानि त्रेतायां पुष्करं परम् ।
द्वापरे तु कुरुक्षेत्रं कलौ गङ्गा विशिष्यते ॥
2.38.m: In the Kṛta age all sacred fords [are efficacious], in the Tretā Puṣkara is supreme, / in the Dvāpara Kurukṣetra, and in the Kali age the Gaṅgā is pre-eminent.

2.38.s:
kalau tu sarvatīrthāni svaṃ svaṃ vīryaṃ svabhāvataḥ /
gaṅgāyāṃ pratimuñcanti sā tu devī na kutracit //
2.38.d:
कलौ तु सर्वतीर्थानि स्वं स्वं वीर्यं स्वभावतः ।
गङ्गायां प्रतिमुञ्चन्ति सा तु देवी न कुत्रचित् ॥
2.38.m: In the Kali age, all sacred fords naturally release their own potency / into the Gaṅgā; but that goddess releases hers nowhere else.

2.38.s:
gaṅgāṃbhaḥ kaṇadigdhasya vāyoḥ saṃsparśanādapi /
pāpaśīlā api narāḥ parāṃ gatimavāpnuyuḥ //
2.38.d:
गङ्गांभः कणदिग्धस्य वायोः संस्पर्शनादपि ।
पापशीला अपि नराः परां गतिमवाप्नुयुः ॥
2.38.m: Even by the touch of the wind smeared with droplets of Gaṅgā water, / even sinful men may attain the supreme destination.

2.38.s:
yo 'sau sarvagato viṣṇuścitsvarūpī janārdanaḥ /
sa eva dravarūpeṇa gaṅgāṃbho nātra saṃśayaḥ //
2.38.d:
यो ऽसौ सर्वगतो विष्णुश्चित्स्वरूपी जनार्दनः ।
स एव द्रवरूपेण गङ्गांभो नात्र संशयः ॥
2.38.m: That all-pervading Viṣṇu, Janārdana whose form is consciousness— / he himself is the water of the Gaṅgā in liquid form; there is no doubt about this.”

2.38.s:
brahmahā guruḍā goghnaḥ steyī ca gurutalpagaḥ /
gaṅgāṃbhasā ca pūyante nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
2.38.d:
ब्रह्महा गुरुडा गोघ्नः स्तेयी च गुरुतल्पगः ।
गङ्गांभसा च पूयन्ते नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
2.38.m:
The killer of a brahmin, the betrayer of a guru, the cow-slayer, the thief, and the violator of the guru's bed
are purified by the water of the Gaṅgā; no doubt should be entertained on this matter.

2.38.s:
kṣetrasthamṛddhṛtaṃ vāpi śītamuṣṇamathāpi vā /
gāṅgeyaṃ tu harettoyaṃ pāpamāmaraṇāntikam //
2.38.d:
क्षेत्रस्थमृद्धृतं वापि शीतमुष्णमथापि वा ।
गाङ्गेयं तु हरेत्तोयं पापमामरणान्तिकम् ॥
2.38.m:
Whether standing in its sacred field or carried [away], whether cold or hot,
the water belonging to the Gaṅgā removes sin up to the moment of death.

2.38.s:
varjyaṃ paryuṣitaṃ toyaṃ varjyaṃ puryuṣitaṃ dalam /
na varjyaṃ jāhnavītoyaṃ na varjyaṃ tulasīdalam //
2.38.d:
वर्ज्यं पर्युषितं तोयं वर्ज्यं पुर्युषितं दलम् ।
न वर्ज्यं जाह्नवीतोयं न वर्ज्यं तुलसीदलम् ॥
2.38.m:
Stale water is to be avoided; a stale leaf is to be avoided;
[but] the water of the Jāhnavī is not to be avoided, and the tulasī leaf is not to be avoided.

2.38.s:
meroḥ suvarṇasya ca sarvaratnaiḥ saṃkhyopalānāmudakasya vāpi /
gaṅgājalānāṃ na tu śaktirasti vaktuṃ guṇākhyāparimāṇamatra //
2.38.d:
मेरोः सुवर्णस्य च सर्वरत्नैः संख्योपलानामुदकस्य वापि ।
गङ्गाजलानां न तु शक्तिरस्ति वक्तुं गुणाख्यापरिमाणमत्र ॥
2.38.m:
There is the capacity to count the stones of Meru and of all gold with its jewels, or of water,
but not to proclaim the measure of the qualities of the waters of the Gaṅgā here.

2.38.s:
tīrthayātrāvidhiṃ kṛtsnamakurvāṇo 'pi yo naraḥ /
gaṅgātoyasya māhātmyātso 'pyatra phalabhāgbhavet //
2.38.d:
तीर्थयात्राविधिं कृत्स्नमकुर्वाणो ऽपि यो नरः ।
गङ्गातोयस्य माहात्म्यात्सो ऽप्यत्र फलभाग्भवेत् ॥
2.38.m:
Even a man who does not perform the entire rite of pilgrimage to sacred fords
would also share in its fruit here through the eulogy of greatness of the Gaṅgā's water.

2.38.s:
cintāmaṇiguṇāccāpi gaṅgāyāstoyabindavaḥ /
viśiṣṭā yatprayacchanti bhaktebhyo vāñchitaṃ phalam //
2.38.d:
चिन्तामणिगुणाच्चापि गङ्गायास्तोयबिन्दवः ।
विशिष्टा यत्प्रयच्छन्ति भक्तेभ्यो वाञ्छितं फलम् ॥
2.38.m:
Drops of the Gaṅgā's water are superior even to the quality of the wish-fulfilling jewel,
since they grant the desired fruit to devotees.

2.38.s:
gaṇḍūṣamātrato bhaktyā sakūdgaṅgāṃbhasā naraḥ /
kāmadhenu stanodbhūtānbhuṅkte divyarasāndivi //
2.38.d:
गण्डूषमात्रतो भक्त्या सकूद्गङ्गांभसा नरः ।
कामधेनु स्तनोद्भूतान्भुङ्क्ते दिव्यरसान्दिवि ॥
2.38.m:
A man who drinks even a mouthful of Gaṅgā water with devotion
enjoys divine juices originating from the udder of the wish-fulfilling cow in heaven.

2.38.s:
śālagrāmaśilāyāṃ yastu gaṅgājalaṃ kṣipet /
apahatya tamastīvraṃ bhāti sūryo yathodaye //
2.38.d:
शालग्रामशिलायां यस्तु गङ्गाजलं क्षिपेत् ।
अपहत्य तमस्तीव्रं भाति सूर्यो यथोदये ॥
2.38.m:
Whoever pours Gaṅgā water upon a Śālagrāma stone
shines like the sun at dawn, having destroyed intense darkness.

2.38.s:
manovākkāyajairgrastaḥ pāpairbahuvidhairapi /
vīkṣya gaṅgāṃ bhavetpūtaḥ puruṣo nātra saṃśayaḥ //
2.38.d:
मनोवाक्कायजैर्ग्रस्तः पापैर्बहुविधैरपि ।
वीक्ष्य गङ्गां भवेत्पूतः पुरुषो नात्र संशयः ॥
2.38.m:
Even a man seized by various kinds of sins born of mind, speech, and body
becomes purified upon seeing the Gaṅgā; there is no doubt about this.

2.38.s:
gaṅgātoyābhiṣiktāṃ tu bhikṣāmaśnāti yaḥ sadā /
sarpavatkañcukaṃ muktvā pāpahīno bhavetsa vai //
2.38.d:
गङ्गातोयाभिषिक्तां तु भिक्षामश्नाति यः सदा ।
सर्पवत्कञ्चुकं मुक्त्वा पापहीनो भवेत्स वै ॥
2.38.m:
Whoever constantly eats alms consecrated with Gaṅgā water
becomes free from sin, casting it off like a snake its slough.

2.38.s:
himavadvindhyasadṛśā rāśayaḥ pāpakarmaṇām /
gaṅgāṃbhasā vinaśyanti viṣṇubhaktyā yathāpadaḥ //
2.38.d:
हिमवद्विन्ध्यसदृशा राशयः पापकर्मणाम् ।
गङ्गांभसा विनश्यन्ति विष्णुभक्त्या यथापदः ॥
2.38.m:
Heaps of sinful deeds resembling the Himavat and Vindhya mountains
perish through Gaṅgā water, just as calamities [perish] through devotion to Viṣṇu.

2.38.s:
praveśamātre gaṅgāyāṃ snānārthaṃ bhaktito nṛṇām /
brahmahatyādipāpāni hāhetyuktvā prayāntyalam //
2.38.d:
प्रवेशमात्रे गङ्गायां स्नानार्थं भक्तितो नृणाम् ।
ब्रह्महत्यादिपापानि हाहेत्युक्त्वा प्रयान्त्यलम् ॥
2.38.m:
Upon men's mere entrance into the Gaṅgā for bathing out of devotion,
sins such as brahmin-murder utterly depart, crying 'Alas, alas!'.

2.38.s:
gaṅgātīre vasennityaṃ gaṅgātoyaṃ pibetsadā /
yaḥ pumānsa vimucyeta pātakaiḥ pūrvasaṃcitaiḥ //
2.38.d:
गङ्गातीरे वसेन्नित्यं गङ्गातोयं पिबेत्सदा ।
यः पुमान्स विमुच्येत पातकैः पूर्वसंचितैः ॥
2.38.m:
A person who always dwells on the riverbank of the Gaṅgā and constantly drinks Gaṅgā water
is freed from sins accumulated in the past.

2.38.s:
yo vai gaṅgāṃ samāśritya nityaṃ tiṣṭhati nirbhayaḥ /
sa eva devairmartyaiśca pūjanīyo maharṣibhiḥ //
2.38.d:
यो वै गङ्गां समाश्रित्य नित्यं तिष्ठति निर्भयः ।
स एव देवैर्मर्त्यैश्च पूजनीयो महर्षिभिः ॥
2.38.m:
He who, having resorted to the Gaṅgā, remains ever fearless,
is worthy of worship by the gods, mortals, and great seers.

2.38.s:
kimaṣṭāṅgena yogena kiṃ tapobhiḥ kimadhvaraiḥ /
vāsa eva hi gaṅgāyāṃ sarvato 'pi viśiṣyate //
2.38.d:
किमष्टाङ्गेन योगेन किं तपोभिः किमध्वरैः ।
वास एव हि गङ्गायां सर्वतो ऽपि विशिष्यते ॥
2.38.m:
What is the use of the eight-limbed yoga? What is the use of austerities? What of sacrificial rites?
Dwelling at the Gaṅgā alone is superior to everything.

2.38.s:
kiṃ yajñairbahubhirjāpyaiḥ kiṃ tapobhirdhanārpaṇaiḥ /
svargamokṣapradā gaṅgā sukhasevyā yataḥ sthitā //
yajñairyamaiśca niyamairdānaiḥ saṃnyāsato 'pi vā /
na tatphalamavāproti gaṅgāṃ sevya yadāpnuyāt //
2.38.d:
किं यज्ञैर्बहुभिर्जाप्यैः किं तपोभिर्धनार्पणैः ।
स्वर्गमोक्षप्रदा गङ्गा सुखसेव्या यतः स्थिता ॥
यज्ञैर्यमैश्च नियमैर्दानैः संन्यासतो ऽपि वा ।
न तत्फलमवाप्रोति गङ्गां सेव्य यदाप्नुयात् ॥
2.38.m:
What is the use of many sacrifices, recitations, austerities, and gifts of wealth,
since the Gaṅgā, easily served, stands granting heaven and liberation?

By sacrifices, self-restraints, observances, gifts, or even renunciation,
one does not obtain that fruit which one obtains having served the Gaṅgā.

2.38.s:
prabhāse gosahastreṇa rāhugraste divākare /
yatphalaṃ labhate martyo gaṅgāyāṃ taddinena vai //
2.38.d:
प्रभासे गोसहस्त्रेण राहुग्रस्ते दिवाकरे ।
यत्फलं लभते मर्त्यो गङ्गायां तद्दिनेन वै ॥
2.38.m:
Whatever fruit a mortal attains at Prabhāsa by [gifting] a thousand cows when the sun is seized by Rāhu,
[he attains] on the Gaṅgā in a single day.

2.38.s:
anyopāyāṃśca yastyaktvā mīkṣakāmaḥ suniścitaḥ /
gaṅgātīre sukhaṃ tiṣṭhetsa vai mokṣasya bhājanam //
2.38.d:
अन्योपायांश्च यस्त्यक्त्वा मीक्षकामः सुनिश्चितः ।
गङ्गातीरे सुखं तिष्ठेत्स वै मोक्षस्य भाजनम् ॥
2.38.m:
He who, having abandoned other means, firmly desirous of liberation,
dwells happily on the riverbank of the Gaṅgā, becomes a worthy vessel for liberation.

2.38.s:
vārāṇasyāṃ viśeṣaṇa gaṅgā sadyastu mokṣadā /
pratimāsaṃ caturdaśyāmaṣṭamyāṃ caiva sarvadā //
2.38.d:
वाराणस्यां विशेषण गङ्गा सद्यस्तु मोक्षदा ।
प्रतिमासं चतुर्दश्यामष्टम्यां चैव सर्वदा ॥
2.38.m:
The Gaṅgā at Vārāṇasī especially grants immediate liberation
every month on the fourteenth and eighth days, at all times.

2.38.s:
gaṅgātīre nivāsaśca yāvajjīvaṃ ca siddhidaḥ /
kṛcchrāṇi sarvadā kṛtvā yatphalaṃ sukhamaśnute //
2.38.d:
गङ्गातीरे निवासश्च यावज्जीवं च सिद्धिदः ।
कृच्छ्राणि सर्वदा कृत्वा यत्फलं सुखमश्नुते ॥
2.38.m:
Dwelling on the riverbank of the Gaṅgā throughout life grants spiritual perfection;
whatever fruit one easily enjoys having always performed severe penances,

2.38.s:
sadā cāndrāyaṇaṃ caiva tallabhejjāhnavītaṭe /
gaṅgāsevāparasyeha divasārddhena yatphalam //
2.38.d:
सदा चान्द्रायणं चैव तल्लभेज्जाह्नवीतटे ।
गङ्गासेवापरस्येह दिवसार्द्धेन यत्फलम् ॥
2.38.m:
and [the fruit of] constant cāndrāyaṇa penance, one obtains that on the bank of the Jāhnavī.
Whatever fruit belongs here to one dedicated to the service of the Gaṅgā in half a day,

2.38.s:
na tacchakyaṃ brahmasute prāptuṃ kratuśatairapi /
sarvayajñatapodānayogasvādhyāyakarmabhiḥ //
2.38.d:
न तच्छक्यं ब्रह्मसुते प्राप्तुं क्रतुशतैरपि ।
सर्वयज्ञतपोदानयोगस्वाध्यायकर्मभिः ॥
2.38.m:
that, O son of Brahmā, cannot be obtained even by hundreds of sacrificial rites,
nor by all sacrifices, austerities, gifts, yogas, and practices of sacred study.

2.38.s:
yatphalaṃ tallabhedbhaktyā gaṅgātīranivāsataḥ /
yatpuṇyaṃ satyavacanairnaiṣṭhikabrahmacāriṇām //
2.38.d:
यत्फलं तल्लभेद्भक्त्या गङ्गातीरनिवासतः ।
यत्पुण्यं सत्यवचनैर्नैष्ठिकब्रह्मचारिणाम् ॥
2.38.m:
Whatever fruit is obtained through devotion from dwelling on the riverbank of the Gaṅgā,
whatever religious merit [is gained] by the truthful speech of lifelong celibates,

2.38.s:
yadagnihotriṇāṃ puṇyaṃ tattu gaṅgānivāsataḥ /
samātṛpitṛdārāṇāṃ kulakoṭimanantakam //
2.38.d:
यदग्निहोत्रिणां पुण्यं तत्तु गङ्गानिवासतः ।
समातृपितृदाराणां कुलकोटिमनन्तकम् ॥
2.38.m:
and whatever religious merit belongs to maintainers of the sacred fire, that indeed [comes] from dwelling at the Gaṅgā;
[it delivers] endless tens of millions of ancestors along with mothers, fathers, and wives.

2.38.s:
gaṅgābhaktistārayate saṃsārārṇavato dhruvam /
saṃtoṣaḥ paramaiśvaryaṃ tattvajñānaṃ sukhātmanām //
2.38.d:
गङ्गाभक्तिस्तारयते संसारार्णवतो ध्रुवम् ।
संतोषः परमैश्वर्यं तत्त्वज्ञानं सुखात्मनाम् ॥
2.38.m:
Devotion to the Gaṅgā certainly carries one across the ocean of worldly existence;
contentment, supreme lordship, and knowledge of truth belong to those of blissful nature.

2.38.s:
vinayācārasaṃpattirgaṅgābhaktasya jāyate /
kṛtakṛtyo bhavenmartyo gaṅgāṃ prāpyaiva kevalam //
2.38.d:
विनयाचारसंपत्तिर्गङ्गाभक्तस्य जायते ।
कृतकृत्यो भवेन्मर्त्यो गङ्गां प्राप्यैव केवलम् ॥
2.38.m:
An abundance of modesty and virtuous conduct arises in a devotee of the Gaṅgā;
a mortal has fulfilled all duties merely by reaching the Gaṅgā.

2.38.s:
tadbhaktastatparaśca syānmṛto vāpi na saṃśayaḥ /
bhaktyā tajjalasaṃsparśī tajjalaṃ pibate ca yaḥ //
2.38.d:
तद्भक्तस्तत्परश्च स्यान्मृतो वापि न संशयः ।
भक्त्या तज्जलसंस्पर्शी तज्जलं पिबते च यः ॥
2.38.m:
One should be devoted to her and dedicated to her, whether alive or dead—there is no doubt;
he who touches her water with devotion and drinks her water,

2.38.s:
anāyāsena hi naro mokṣo pāyaṃ sa vindati /
dīkṣitaḥ sarvayajñeṣu somapānaṃ dine dine //
2.38.d:
अनायासेन हि नरो मोक्षो पायं स विन्दति ।
दीक्षितः सर्वयज्ञेषु सोमपानं दिने दिने ॥
2.38.m:
that man easily finds the means to liberation.
He is consecrated in all sacrifices, drinking soma day after day.

2.38.s:
sarvāṇi yaṃṣāṃ gaṅgāyāstoyaiḥ kṛtyāni sarvadā /
dehaṃ tyaktvā narāste tu modante śivasannidhau //
2.38.d:
सर्वाणि यंषां गङ्गायास्तोयैः कृत्यानि सर्वदा ।
देहं त्यक्त्वा नरास्ते तु मोदन्ते शिवसन्निधौ ॥
2.38.m:
Those men all of whose ritual duties are ever [performed] with the waters of the Gaṅgā,
having cast off the body, rejoice in the presence of Śiva.

2.38.s:
devāḥ somārkasaṃsthāni yathā śakrādayo mukhaiḥ /
amṛtānyupabhuñjanti tathā gaṅgājalaṃ narāḥ //
2.38.d:
देवाः सोमार्कसंस्थानि यथा शक्रादयो मुखैः ।
अमृतान्युपभुञ्जन्ति तथा गङ्गाजलं नराः ॥
2.38.m:
Just as gods such as Śakra consume with their mouths the nectars
residing in the moon and the sun, so do men [consume] Gaṅgā water.

2.38.s:
kanyādānaiśca vidhivadbhūmidānaiśca bhaktitaḥ /
annadānaiśca godānaiḥ svarṇadānādibhistathā //
2.38.d:
कन्यादानैश्च विधिवद्भूमिदानैश्च भक्तितः ।
अन्नदानैश्च गोदानैः स्वर्णदानादिभिस्तथा ॥
2.38.m:
By gifts of a maiden in marriage according to rule, by gifts of land with devotion,
by gifts of food, by gifts of cows, and likewise by gifts of gold and the like,

2.38.s:
rathāśvagajadānaiśca yatpuṇyaṃ parikīrtitam /
tataḥ śataguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ gaṅgāṃbhaśculukāśanāt //
2.38.d:
रथाश्वगजदानैश्च यत्पुण्यं परिकीर्तितम् ।
ततः शतगुणं पुण्यं गङ्गांभश्चुलुकाशनात् ॥
2.38.m:
and by gifts of chariots, horses, and elephants, whatever religious merit is proclaimed—
a hundred times that merit [arises] from drinking a handful of Gaṅgā water.

2.38.s:
cāndrāyaṇasahasrāṇāṃ yatphalaṃ parikīrtitam /
tato 'dhikaphalaṃ gaṅgātoyapānādavāpyate //
2.38.d:
चान्द्रायणसहस्राणां यत्फलं परिकीर्तितम् ।
ततो ऽधिकफलं गङ्गातोयपानादवाप्यते ॥
2.38.m:
Whatever fruit is proclaimed for thousands of cāndrāyaṇa penances,
a fruit greater than that is obtained from drinking Gaṅgā water.

2.38.s:
gaṇḍūṣamātrapāne tu aśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet /
svacchandaṃ yaḥ pibedaṃbhastasya muktiḥ kare sthitā //
2.38.d:
गण्डूषमात्रपाने तु अश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ।
स्वच्छन्दं यः पिबेदंभस्तस्य मुक्तिः करे स्थिता ॥
2.38.m:
From drinking merely a mouthful, one obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice;
for him who drinks its water freely, liberation rests in his hand.

2.38.s:
tribhiḥ sārasvataṃ toyaṃ saptabhistvatha yāmunam /
nārmadaṃ daśabhirmāsairgāṅgaṃ varṣeṇa jīryati //
2.38.d:
त्रिभिः सारस्वतं तोयं सप्तभिस्त्वथ यामुनम् ।
नार्मदं दशभिर्मासैर्गाङ्गं वर्षेण जीर्यति ॥
2.38.m:
The water of the Sarasvatī is digested in three days, but that of the Yamunā in seven,
that of the Narmadā in ten months, [and] that of the Gaṅgā in a year.

2.38.s:
śāstreṇākṛtatoyānāṃ mṛtānāṃ kvāpi dehanām /
taduttaraphalāvāptirgaṅgāyāmasthiyogataḥ //
2.38.d:
शास्त्रेणाकृततोयानां मृतानां क्वापि देहनाम् ।
तदुत्तरफलावाप्तिर्गङ्गायामस्थियोगतः ॥
2.38.m:
For embodied beings who have died anywhere without water rites performed according to scripture,
the attainment of higher fruits follows from the contact of their bones with the Gaṅgā.

2.38.s:
cāndrāyaṇasahasraṃ tu yaścaretkāyaśodhanam /
yaḥ pibettu yatheṣṭhaṃ hi gaṅgāmbhaḥ sa viśiṣyate //
2.38.d:
चान्द्रायणसहस्रं तु यश्चरेत्कायशोधनम् ।
यः पिबेत्तु यथेष्ठं हि गङ्गाम्भः स विशिष्यते ॥
2.38.m:
He who might practice a thousand cāndrāyaṇa penances to purify the body—
he who drinks Gaṅgā water to his heart's content is superior.

2.38.s:
gaṅgāṃ paśyati yaḥ stauti snāti bhaktyā pibejjalam /
sa svargaṃ jñānamamalaṃ yogaṃ mokṣaṃ ca vindati //
2.38.d:
गङ्गां पश्यति यः स्तौति स्नाति भक्त्या पिबेज्जलम् ।
स स्वर्गं ज्ञानममलं योगं मोक्षं च विन्दति ॥
2.38.m:
He who looks upon the Gaṅgā, praises her, bathes with devotion, and drinks her water
attains heaven, spotless knowledge, yoga, and liberation.

2.38.s:
yastu sūryyāṃśuniṣṭaptaṃ gāṅgeyaṃ pibate jalam /
gomūtrayāvakāhārādgāṅgapānaṃ viśiṣyate //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇottarabhāge mohinīvasusaṃvāde gaṅgāmāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmāṣṭatriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.38.d:
यस्तु सूर्य्यांशुनिष्टप्तं गाङ्गेयं पिबते जलम् ।
गोमूत्रयावकाहाराद्गाङ्गपानं विशिष्यते ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणोत्तरभागे मोहिनीवसुसंवादे गङ्गामाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामाष्टत्रिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
2.38.m:
He who drinks Gaṅgā water heated by the rays of the sun—
drinking Gaṅgā water is superior to a diet of cow's urine and barley.

Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter named 'Description of the Eulogy of Greatness of the Gaṅgā' in the conversation between Mohinī and Vasu, in the latter section of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

2.39.s:
vasuruvāca
śṛṇu mohini vakṣyāmi gaṅgāyā darśane phalam /
yaduktaṃ hi purāṇeṣu munibhistattvadarśibhiḥ //
2.39.d:
वसुरुवाच
शृणु मोहिनि वक्ष्यामि गङ्गाया दर्शने फलम् ।
यदुक्तं हि पुराणेषु मुनिभिस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥
2.39.m:
Vasu said:
Listen, O Mohinī, I will explain the fruit of seeing the Gaṅgā
which has been spoken in the Purāṇas by the seers who see truth.

2.39.s:
bhavanti nirviṣāḥ sarpā yathā tārkṣyasya daśa nāt /
gaṅgāsaṃdarśanāttadvatsarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate //
2.39.d:
भवन्ति निर्विषाः सर्पा यथा तार्क्ष्यस्य दश नात् ।
गङ्गासंदर्शनात्तद्वत्सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
2.39.m:
Just as serpents become venomless upon the sight of Garuḍa,
even so one is freed from all sins upon the sight of the Gaṅgā.

2.39.s:
saptāvarān saptaparān pitṛṃstebhyaśca ye pare /
pumāṃstārayate gaṅgāṃ vīkṣya spṛṣṭvāvagāhya ca //
2.39.d:
सप्तावरान् सप्तपरान् पितृंस्तेभ्यश्च ये परे ।
पुमांस्तारयते गङ्गां वीक्ष्य स्पृष्ट्वावगाह्य च ॥
2.39.m:
Looking upon, touching, and bathing in the Gaṅgā,
a man delivers seven subsequent and seven prior ancestors, and those beyond them.

2.39.s:
darśanātsparśanātpānāttathā gaṅgeti kīrtanāt /
pumānpunāti puruṣāñchataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ //
2.39.d:
दर्शनात्स्पर्शनात्पानात्तथा गङ्गेति कीर्तनात् ।
पुमान्पुनाति पुरुषाञ्छतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
2.39.m:
From seeing, touching, drinking, and chanting 'Gaṅgā',
a man purifies men by the hundreds and thousands.

2.39.s:
jñānamaiśvaryamatulaṃ pratiṣṭhāyuryaśastathā /
śubhānāmāśramāṇāṃ ca gaṅgādarśanajaṃ phalam //
2.39.d:
ज्ञानमैश्वर्यमतुलं प्रतिष्ठायुर्यशस्तथा ।
शुभानामाश्रमाणां च गङ्गादर्शनजं फलम् ॥
2.39.m:
Knowledge, matchless lordship, status, long life, fame,
and auspicious life-stages are the fruit born of seeing the Gaṅgā.

2.39.s:
sarvendriyāṇāṃ cāñcalyaṃ vyasanāni ca pātakam /
nirghṛṇatvaṃ ca naśyanti gaṅgādarśana mātrataḥ //
2.39.d:
सर्वेन्द्रियाणां चाञ्चल्यं व्यसनानि च पातकम् ।
निर्घृणत्वं च नश्यन्ति गङ्गादर्शन मात्रतः ॥
2.39.m: Restlessness of all the senses, vices, and sin, / and cruelty—all perish merely by the sight of the Gaṅgā.

2.39.s:
parahiṃsā ca kauṭilyaṃ paradoṣādyavekṣaṇam /
dāṃbhikatvaṃ nṛṇāṃ gaṅgādarśanādeva naśyati //
2.39.d:
परहिंसा च कौटिल्यं परदोषाद्यवेक्षणम् ।
दांभिकत्वं नृणां गङ्गादर्शनादेव नश्यति ॥
2.39.m: Harming others, crookedness, looking for others' faults, / and hypocrisy among men perish just by the sight of the Gaṅgā.

2.39.s:
muhurmuhustathā paśyetspṛśedvāpi muhurmuhuḥ /
bhaktyā yadicchati naraḥ śāśvataṃ padamavyayam //
2.39.d:
मुहुर्मुहुस्तथा पश्येत्स्पृशेद्वापि मुहुर्मुहुः ।
भक्त्या यदिच्छति नरः शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ॥
2.39.m: One should look [upon her] again and again, or touch [her] again and again, / with devotion, if a man desires the eternal, imperishable abode.

2.39.s:
vāpīkūpataḍāgādiprapāsatrādibhistathā /
anyatra yadbhavetpuṇyaṃ tadgaṅgādarśanādbhavet //
2.39.d:
वापीकूपतडागादिप्रपासत्रादिभिस्तथा ।
अन्यत्र यद्भवेत्पुण्यं तद्गङ्गादर्शनाद्भवेत् ॥
2.39.m: Whatever merit might be obtained elsewhere through step-wells, wells, ponds, / water-sheds, free feeding-houses, and the like, is gained by the sight of the Gaṅgā.

2.39.s:
yatphalaṃ jāyate puṃsāṃ darśane paramātmanaḥ /
tadbhavedeva gaṅgāyā darśanādbhaktibhāvataḥ //
2.39.d:
यत्फलं जायते पुंसां दर्शने परमात्मनः ।
तद्भवेदेव गङ्गाया दर्शनाद्भक्तिभावतः ॥
2.39.m: Whatever fruit is produced for men by the sight of the Supreme Self, / that indeed comes from the sight of the Gaṅgā with a devotional attitude.

2.39.s:
naimiṣe ca kurukṣetre narmadāyāṃ ca puṣkare /
snānātsaṃsparśanā sevya yatphalaṃ labhate naraḥ //
2.39.d:
नैमिषे च कुरुक्षेत्रे नर्मदायां च पुष्करे ।
स्नानात्संस्पर्शना सेव्य यत्फलं लभते नरः ॥
2.39.m: Whatever fruit a man obtains at Naimiṣa, Kurukṣetra, / at the Narmadā, and at Puṣkara by bathing, touching, or serving,

2.39.s:
tadgaṅgādarśanādeva kalau prāhurmaharṣayaḥ /
atha te smaraṇasyāpi gaṅgāyā bhūpabhāmini //
2.39.d:
तद्गङ्गादर्शनादेव कलौ प्राहुर्महर्षयः ।
अथ ते स्मरणस्यापि गङ्गाया भूपभामिनि ॥
2.39.m: great sages say that in the Kali [age] is gained merely by the sight of the Gaṅgā. / Now, O beautiful queen, I shall tell you the fruit even of remembering the Gaṅgā,

2.39.s:
pravakṣyāmi phalaṃ yattu purāṇeṣu prakīrtitam /
aśubhaiḥ karmabhiryuktānmajjamānānbhavārṇave //
2.39.d:
प्रवक्ष्यामि फलं यत्तु पुराणेषु प्रकीर्तितम् ।
अशुभैः कर्मभिर्युक्तान्मज्जमानान्भवार्णवे ॥
2.39.m: which is proclaimed in the Purāṇas. / Even those bound by inauspicious deeds, sinking in the ocean of worldly existence,

2.39.s:
patato narake gaṅgā smṛtā dūrātsamuddharet /
yojanānāṃ sahasreṣu gaṅgāṃ smarati yo naraḥ //
2.39.d:
पततो नरके गङ्गा स्मृता दूरात्समुद्धरेत् ।
योजनानां सहस्रेषु गङ्गां स्मरति यो नरः ॥
2.39.m: and falling into hell, the Gaṅgā delivers from afar when remembered. / The man who remembers the Gaṅgā even from a thousand yojanas,

2.39.s:
api duṣkṛtakarmā hi labhate paramāṃ gatim /
smaraṇādeva gaṅgāyāḥ pāpasaṃghātapañjaram //
2.39.d:
अपि दुष्कृतकर्मा हि लभते परमां गतिम् ।
स्मरणादेव गङ्गायाः पापसंघातपञ्जरम् ॥
2.39.m: even if he is an evildoer, attains the supreme destination. / Merely by remembering the Gaṅgā, the cage formed of accumulated sins

2.39.s:
bhedaṃ sahasradhā yāti girirvajrahato yathā /
gacchaṃstiṣṭhansvapandhyāyañjāgradbhuñjan hasan rudan //
2.39.d:
भेदं सहस्रधा याति गिरिर्वज्रहतो यथा ।
गच्छंस्तिष्ठन्स्वपन्ध्यायञ्जाग्रद्भुञ्जन् हसन् रुदन् ॥
2.39.m: is shattered in a thousand ways, like a mountain struck by a thunderbolt. / Walking, standing, sleeping, meditating, waking, eating, laughing, or weeping,

2.39.s:
yaḥ smaretsatataṃ gaṅgāṃ sa ca mucyeta bandhanāt /
sahasrayojanasthāśca gaṅgāṃ bhaktyā smaranti ye //
2.39.d:
यः स्मरेत्सततं गङ्गां स च मुच्येत बन्धनात् ।
सहस्रयोजनस्थाश्च गङ्गां भक्त्या स्मरन्ति ये ॥
2.39.m: whoever constantly remembers the Gaṅgā is freed from bondage. / And those who, situated a thousand yojanas away, remember the Gaṅgā with devotion,

2.39.s:
gaṅgāgaṅgeti cākruśya mucyante te 'pi pātakāt /
ye ca smaranti vai gaṅgāṃ gaṅgābhaktiparāśca ye //
2.39.d:
गङ्गागङ्गेति चाक्रुश्य मुच्यन्ते ते ऽपि पातकात् ।
ये च स्मरन्ति वै गङ्गां गङ्गाभक्तिपराश्च ये ॥
2.39.m: and cry out, 'Gaṅgā! Gaṅgā!', are also freed from sin. / And those who remember the Gaṅgā and are intent upon devotion to the Gaṅgā,

2.39.s:
te 'pyaśeṣairmahāpāpairmucyante nātra saṃśayaḥ /
bhavanāni vicitrāṇi vicitrābharaṇāḥ striyaḥ //
2.39.d:
ते ऽप्यशेषैर्महापापैर्मुच्यन्ते नात्र संशयः ।
भवनानि विचित्राणि विचित्राभरणाः स्त्रियः ॥
2.39.m: are freed from all great sins; of this there is no doubt. / Splendid mansions, women adorned with varied ornaments,

2.39.s:
ārogyaṃ vittrasaṃpattirgaṅgāsmaraṇañja phalam /
manasā saṃsmaredyastu gaṅgāṃ dūrasthito naraḥ //
2.39.d:
आरोग्यं वित्त्रसंपत्तिर्गङ्गास्मरणञ्ज फलम् ।
मनसा संस्मरेद्यस्तु गङ्गां दूरस्थितो नरः ॥
2.39.m: health, and abundance of wealth are the fruit born of remembering the Gaṅgā. / But that man who, standing far away, remembers the Gaṅgā in his mind,

2.39.s:
cāndrāyaṇasahasrasya sa phalaṃ labhate dhruvam /
gaṅgā gaṅgā japannāma yojanānāṃ śate sthitaḥ //
2.39.d:
चान्द्रायणसहस्रस्य स फलं लभते ध्रुवम् ।
गङ्गा गङ्गा जपन्नाम योजनानां शते स्थितः ॥
2.39.m: certainly obtains the fruit of a thousand cāndrāyaṇa penances. / Repeating the name 'Gaṅgā, Gaṅgā', though situated a hundred yojanas away,

2.39.s:
mucyate sarvapāpebhyo viṣṇulokaṃ ca gacchati /
kīrtanānmucyate pāpāddarśanānmaṅgalaṃ labhet //
2.39.d:
मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो विष्णुलोकं च गच्छति ।
कीर्तनान्मुच्यते पापाद्दर्शनान्मङ्गलं लभेत् ॥
2.39.m: he is freed from all sins and goes to the world of Viṣṇu. / By chanting [her name] one is freed from sin; by seeing [her] one attains auspiciousness;

2.39.s:
avagāhya tathā pītvā punātyāsaptamaṃ kulam /
saptāvaparānparānsapta saptātha parataḥ parān //
2.39.d:
अवगाह्य तथा पीत्वा पुनात्यासप्तमं कुलम् ।
सप्तावपरान्परान्सप्त सप्ताथ परतः परान् ॥
2.39.m: by plunging [into her] and drinking [her water], one purifies up to the seventh generation of one's family. / Seven prior, seven later, and then seven beyond those—

2.39.s:
gaṅgā tārayate puṃsāṃ prasaṃgenāpi kīrtitā /
aśraddhayāpi gaṅgāyā yattu nāmānukīrtanam //
2.39.d:
गङ्गा तारयते पुंसां प्रसंगेनापि कीर्तिता ।
अश्रद्धयापि गङ्गाया यत्तु नामानुकीर्तनम् ॥
2.39.m: the Gaṅgā delivers [the ancestors] of men, even if praised only incidentally. / The recitation of the name of the river of merit, the Gaṅgā,

2.39.s:
karoti puṇyavāhinyāḥ so 'pi svargasya bhājanam /
sarvāvasthāṃ gato vāpi sarvadharmavivarjitaḥ //
2.39.d:
करोति पुण्यवाहिन्याः सो ऽपि स्वर्गस्य भाजनम् ।
सर्वावस्थां गतो वापि सर्वधर्मविवर्जितः ॥
2.39.m: which one performs even without faith, makes even him a receptacle of heaven. / Or, even if fallen into any condition, completely devoid of all religious duties,

2.39.s:
gaṅgāyāḥ kīrtanenaiva śubhāṃ gatimavāpnuyāt /
brahmahā guruhāgoghnaḥ spṛṣṭo vā sarvapātakaiḥ //
2.39.d:
गङ्गायाः कीर्तनेनैव शुभां गतिमवाप्नुयात् ।
ब्रह्महा गुरुहागोघ्नः स्पृष्टो वा सर्वपातकैः ॥
2.39.m: merely by praising the Gaṅgā one attains an auspicious destination. / A killer of a brāhmaṇa, a killer of a guru, a cow-slayer, or one tainted by all sins,

2.39.s:
gaṅgātoyaṃ naraḥ spṛṣṭvā mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ /
kadā drakṣyāmi tāṃ gaṅgāṃ kadā snānaṃ labhe hyaham //
2.39.d:
गङ्गातोयं नरः स्पृष्ट्वा मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः ।
कदा द्रक्ष्यामि तां गङ्गां कदा स्नानं लभे ह्यहम् ॥
2.39.m: having touched the water of the Gaṅgā, a man is freed from all sins. / 'When shall I see that Gaṅgā? When indeed shall I obtain a bath?'—

2.39.s:
iti puṃsābhilaṣitā kulānāṃ tārayecchatam /
atha snānaphalaṃ devi gaṅgāyāḥ pravadāmi te //
2.39.d:
इति पुंसाभिलषिता कुलानां तारयेच्छतम् ।
अथ स्नानफलं देवि गङ्गायाः प्रवदामि ते ॥
2.39.m: desired in this way by a man, she delivers a hundred [generations] of his family. / Now, O goddess, I shall declare to you the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā,

2.39.s:
yacchrutvā sarvapāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ /
snātasya gaṅgāsalile sadyaḥ pāpaṃ praṇaśyati //
2.39.d:
यच्छ्रुत्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ।
स्नातस्य गङ्गासलिले सद्यः पापं प्रणश्यति ॥
2.39.m: hearing which one is freed from all sins; of this there is no doubt. / The sin of one who has bathed in the water of the Gaṅgā instantly perishes,

2.39.s:
apūrvapuṇyaprāptiśca sadyo mohini jāyate /
snātānāṃ śucibhistoyairgāṅgeyaiḥ prayatātmanām //
2.39.d:
अपूर्वपुण्यप्राप्तिश्च सद्यो मोहिनि जायते ।
स्नातानां शुचिभिस्तोयैर्गाङ्गेयैः प्रयतात्मनाम् ॥
2.39.m: and unprecedented merit is instantly generated, O Mohinī. / For men of restrained minds who have bathed in the pure waters of the Gaṅgā,

2.39.s:
vyuṣṭirbhavati yā puṃsāṃ na sā kratuśatairapi /
apahatya tamastīvraṃ yathā bhātyudaye raviḥ //
2.39.d:
व्युष्टिर्भवति या पुंसां न सा क्रतुशतैरपि ।
अपहत्य तमस्तीव्रं यथा भात्युदये रविः ॥
2.39.m: whatever reward accrues is not [attained] even by hundreds of sacrifices. / Just as the sun shines at dawn, dispelling intense darkness,

2.39.s:
tathāpahatya pāpmānaṃ bhāti gaṅgājalokṣitaḥ /
ekenaivāpi vidhinā snānena nṛpasundari //
2.39.d:
तथापहत्य पाप्मानं भाति गङ्गाजलोक्षितः ।
एकेनैवापि विधिना स्नानेन नृपसुन्दरि ॥
2.39.m: so one sprinkled with the water of the Gaṅgā shines, dispelling evil. / Even by a single bath according to the rule, O king's beautiful lady,

2.39.s:
aśvamedhaphalaṃ martyo gaṅgāyāṃ labhate dhruvam /
anekajanmasaṃbhūtaṃ puṃsaḥ pāpaṃ praṇaśyati //
2.39.d:
अश्वमेधफलं मर्त्यो गङ्गायां लभते ध्रुवम् ।
अनेकजन्मसंभूतं पुंसः पापं प्रणश्यति ॥
2.39.m: a mortal certainly attains the fruit of an aśvamedha sacrifice in the Gaṅgā. / A man's sin born of many lifetimes perishes;

2.39.s:
snānamātreṇa gaṅgāyāḥ sadyaḥ syātpuṇyabhājanam /
anyasthānakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ gaṅgātīre vinaśyati //
2.39.d:
स्नानमात्रेण गङ्गायाः सद्यः स्यात्पुण्यभाजनम् ।
अन्यस्थानकृतं पापं गङ्गातीरे विनश्यति ॥
2.39.m: merely by bathing in the Gaṅgā he instantly becomes a vessel of merit. / Sin committed in another place perishes on the riverbank of the Gaṅgā;

2.39.s:
gaṅgātīre kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ gaṅgāsnānena naśyati /
rātrau divā ca saṃdhyāyāṃ gaṅgāyāṃ tu prayatnataḥ //
2.39.d:
गङ्गातीरे कृतं पापं गङ्गास्नानेन नश्यति ।
रात्रौ दिवा च संध्यायां गङ्गायां तु प्रयत्नतः ॥
2.39.m: sin committed on the riverbank of the Gaṅgā perishes by a bath in the Gaṅgā. / By diligently bathing in the Gaṅgā by night, by day, and at twilight,

2.39.s:
snātvāśvamedhajaṃ puṇyaṃ gṛhe 'pyuddhṛtatatajjalaiḥ /
sarvatīrtheṣu yatpuṇyaṃ sarveṣṭāyataneṣu ca //
2.39.d:
स्नात्वाश्वमेधजं पुण्यं गृहे ऽप्युद्धृतततज्जलैः ।
सर्वतीर्थेषु यत्पुण्यं सर्वेष्टायतनेषु च ॥
2.39.m: or even at home with waters brought from it, [one obtains] the merit born of an aśvamedha. / Whatever merit [is gained] at all sacred fords and in all sacred sanctuaries,

2.39.s:
tatphalaṃ labhate martyo gaṅgāsnānānna saṃśayaḥ /
mahāpātakasaṃyukto yukto vā sarvapātakaiḥ //
2.39.d:
तत्फलं लभते मर्त्यो गङ्गास्नानान्न संशयः ।
महापातकसंयुक्तो युक्तो वा सर्वपातकैः ॥
2.39.m: that fruit a mortal obtains from a bath in the Gaṅgā; there is no doubt. / Whether joined with a great sin or joined with all sins,

2.39.s:
gaṅgāsnānena vidhivanmucyate sarvapātakaiḥ /
gaṅgā snānātparaṃ snānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati //
2.39.d:
गङ्गास्नानेन विधिवन्मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः ।
गङ्गा स्नानात्परं स्नानं न भूतं न भविष्यति ॥
2.39.m: by bathing in the Gaṅgā according to the rule one is freed from all sins. / There has been no bath superior to a bath in the Gaṅgā, nor will there ever be.

2.39.s:
viśeṣataḥ kaliyuge pāpaṃ harati jāhnavī /
nihatya kāmajāndoṣānkāyavākcittasaṃbhavān //
2.39.d:
विशेषतः कलियुगे पापं हरति जाह्नवी ।
निहत्य कामजान्दोषान्कायवाक्चित्तसंभवान् ॥
2.39.m: Especially in the Kali age, the Jāhnavī removes sin, / having destroyed the faults born of desire that arise from body, speech, and mind.

2.39.s:
gaṅgāsnānena bhaktyā tu modate divi devavat /
varṣaṃ snāti ca gaṅgāyāṃ yo naro bhaktisaṃyutaḥ //
2.39.d:
गङ्गास्नानेन भक्त्या तु मोदते दिवि देववत् ।
वर्षं स्नाति च गङ्गायां यो नरो भक्तिसंयुतः ॥
2.39.m: By bathing in the Gaṅgā with devotion, one rejoices in heaven like a god. / And the man who, endowed with devotion, bathes in the Gaṅgā for a year—

2.39.s:
tasya syādvaiṣṇave loke sthitiḥ kalpaṃ na saṃśayaḥ /
āmṛtyuṃ snāti gaṅgāyāṃ yo naro nityameva ca //
2.39.d:
तस्य स्याद्वैष्णवे लोके स्थितिः कल्पं न संशयः ।
आमृत्युं स्नाति गङ्गायां यो नरो नित्यमेव च ॥
2.39.m: his residence will be in the world of Viṣṇu for a kalpa; there is no doubt. / The man who always bathes in the Gaṅgā until death,

2.39.s:
samastapāpanimuktaḥ samastakulasaṃyutaḥ /
samastabhogasaṃyukto viṣṇuloke mahīyate //
2.39.d:
समस्तपापनिमुक्तः समस्तकुलसंयुतः ।
समस्तभोगसंयुक्तो विष्णुलोके महीयते ॥
2.39.m: freed from all sins, accompanied by all his family, / and endowed with all enjoyments, is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu

2.39.s:
parārddhadvitayaṃ yāvannātra kāryā vicāraṇā /
gaṅgāyāṃ snāti yo martyo nairantaryeṇa nityadā //
2.39.d:
परार्द्धद्वितयं यावन्नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।
गङ्गायां स्नाति यो मर्त्यो नैरन्तर्येण नित्यदा ॥
2.39.m: for two parārdhas; no deliberation should be made here. / That mortal who constantly and uninterruptedly bathes in the Gaṅgā

2.39.s:
jīvanmuktaḥ sa cātraiva mṛto viṣṇupadaṃ vrajet /
prātaḥsnānāddaśaguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ madhyandine smṛtam //
2.39.d:
जीवन्मुक्तः स चात्रैव मृतो विष्णुपदं व्रजेत् ।
प्रातःस्नानाद्दशगुणं पुण्यं मध्यन्दिने स्मृतम् ॥
2.39.m: is liberated while living right here, and, when dead, goes to the abode of Viṣṇu. / Compared to a morning bath, the merit is taught to be tenfold at midday,

2.39.s:
sāyaṅkāle śataguṇamanantaṃ śivasannidhau /
kapilākoṭidānāddhi gaṅgāsnānaṃ viśiṣyate //
2.39.d:
सायङ्काले शतगुणमनन्तं शिवसन्निधौ ।
कपिलाकोटिदानाद्धि गङ्गास्नानं विशिष्यते ॥
2.39.m: a hundredfold in the evening, and infinite in the presence of Śiva. / Indeed, bathing in the Gaṅgā is superior to the gift of ten million brown cows.

2.39.s:
kurukṣetrasamā gaṅgā yatra tatrāvagāhitā /
haridvāre prayāge ca siṃdhusaṃge phalādhikā //
2.39.d:
कुरुक्षेत्रसमा गङ्गा यत्र तत्रावगाहिता ।
हरिद्वारे प्रयागे च सिंधुसंगे फलाधिका ॥
2.39.m: Wherever bathed in, the Gaṅgā is equal to Kurukṣetra; / at Haridvāra, at Prayāga, and at the confluence with the ocean, her fruit is even greater.

2.39.s:
ye madīyāṃśusaṃtapte jale te snānti jāhnavi /
te bhitvā maṇḍalaṃ yānti mokṣaṃ ceti ravervacaḥ //
2.39.d:
ये मदीयांशुसंतप्ते जले ते स्नान्ति जाह्नवि ।
ते भित्वा मण्डलं यान्ति मोक्षं चेति रवेर्वचः ॥
2.39.m: 'Those who bathe in your water heated by my rays, O Jāhnavī, / pierce the [solar] orb and go to liberation'—such is the word of the Sun.

2.39.s:
yo gṛhe sve sthito 'pi tvāṃ snāne saṃkīrtayiṣyati /
so 'pi yāsyati nākaṃ vai ityāha varuṇaśca tām //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇottarabhāge mohinīcarite gaṅgāsnānamāhātmyaṃ nāmaikonacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.39.d:
यो गृहे स्वे स्थितो ऽपि त्वां स्नाने संकीर्तयिष्यति ।
सो ऽपि यास्यति नाकं वै इत्याह वरुणश्च ताम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणोत्तरभागे मोहिनीचरिते गङ्गास्नानमाहात्म्यं नामैकोनचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
2.39.m:
'Whoever, even while staying in his own home, will chant your name during his bath, / he too shall go to heaven'—thus said Varuṇa to her.

Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, entitled 'The Eulogy of the Greatness of Bathing in the Gaṅgā', in the story of Mohinī in the Uttarabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

2.40.s:
vasuruvāca
atha kālaviśeṣe tu gaṅgāsnānasya te phalam /
kīrtayiṣyāmi vāmoru sāvadhānā niśāmaya //
2.40.d:
वसुरुवाच
अथ कालविशेषे तु गङ्गास्नानस्य ते फलम् ।
कीर्तयिष्यामि वामोरु सावधाना निशामय ॥
2.40.m: Vasu said: / Now I shall proclaim to you the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā at specific times, / O fair-thighed lady; listen attentively.

2.40.s:
nairantaryeṇa gaṅgāyā māghe snāti ca yo naraḥ /
saśakraloke suciraṃ kālaṃ tiṣṭhetsagotrajaḥ //
2.40.d:
नैरन्तर्येण गङ्गाया माघे स्नाति च यो नरः ।
सशक्रलोके सुचिरं कालं तिष्ठेत्सगोत्रजः ॥
2.40.m: The man who bathes in the Gaṅgā without interruption during the month of Māgha / shall reside in the world of Indra for a very long time together with his kinsmen.

2.40.s:
tato brahmapuraṃ yāti kalpakoṭiśatāyutaiḥ /
nairantaryeṇa vidhivadgaṅgāyāṃ snāti yo naraḥ //
2.40.d:
ततो ब्रह्मपुरं याति कल्पकोटिशतायुतैः ।
नैरन्तर्येण विधिवद्गङ्गायां स्नाति यो नरः ॥
2.40.m: Then he goes to the city of Brahmā for hundreds of tens of millions of kalpas— / the man who uninterruptedly bathes in the Gaṅgā according to the rule.

2.40.s:
ṣaṇmāsa mekakālāśī sakṛdevottarāyaṇe /
so 'pi viṣṇupadaṃ yāti kulānāṃ śatamuddharan //
2.40.d:
षण्मास मेककालाशी सकृदेवोत्तरायणे ।
सो ऽपि विष्णुपदं याति कुलानां शतमुद्धरन् ॥
2.40.m: Eating once a day for six months, [or] just once during the northern solstice, / he too goes to the abode of Viṣṇu, uplifting a hundred of his families.

2.40.s:
saṃkrāntiṣu tu sarvāsu snātvā gaṅgājale naraḥ /
vimānenārkavarṇena sa vrajedviṣṇumandiram //
2.40.d:
संक्रान्तिषु तु सर्वासु स्नात्वा गङ्गाजले नरः ।
विमानेनार्कवर्णेन स व्रजेद्विष्णुमन्दिरम् ॥
2.40.m: A man who bathes in the water of the Gaṅgā on all solar transits / goes to Viṣṇu's dwelling in a sun-bright aerial chariot.

2.40.s:
viṣuve 'yanasaṃkrāntau viśeṣātphalamīritam /
tapaḥsamaṃ kārtike 'pi gaṅgāsnāne phalaṃ viduḥ //
2.40.d:
विषुवे ऽयनसंक्रान्तौ विशेषात्फलमीरितम् ।
तपःसमं कार्तिके ऽपि गङ्गास्नाने फलं विदुः ॥
2.40.m: On the equinox and solstice transits, especially, the fruit is declared [great]; / bathing in the Gaṅgā in Kārtika as well is known to yield a fruit equal to austerity.

2.40.s:
meṣapraveśārkakāle kārtikyāṃ vāpi mohini /
māghasnānādhikaṃ prāhuḥ kamalāsanapūrvakāḥ //
2.40.d:
मेषप्रवेशार्ककाले कार्तिक्यां वापि मोहिनि ।
माघस्नानाधिकं प्राहुः कमलासनपूर्वकाः ॥
2.40.m: At the time of the sun's entry into Aries, or on the full moon of Kārtika, O Mohinī, / Brahmā and the others declare it greater than bathing in Māgha.

2.40.s:
saṃvatsarasnānajanyaṃ phalamakṣayake tithau /
kārtike vāpi vaiśākhe iti prāha pitā tava //
2.40.d:
संवत्सरस्नानजन्यं फलमक्षयके तिथौ ।
कार्तिके वापि वैशाखे इति प्राह पिता तव ॥
2.40.m: The fruit produced by a whole year's bathing is obtained on the inexhaustible lunar day, / whether in Kārtika or in Vaiśākha—so your father declared.

2.40.s:
manvādau ca yugādau yatproktaṃ gaṅgājale phalam /
snānaina yājyavanite trimāsyāpi ca tatphalam //
2.40.d:
मन्वादौ च युगादौ यत्प्रोक्तं गङ्गाजले फलम् ।
स्नानैन याज्यवनिते त्रिमास्यापि च तत्फलम् ॥
2.40.m: Whatever fruit is proclaimed for bathing in the Gaṅgā's water at the start of a Manu-era or world-age, / O sacrificer's wife, that same fruit is also [obtained] by three months [of bathing].

2.40.s:
dvādaśyāṃ śravaṇarkṣe ca aṣṭabhyāṃ puṣyayogataḥ /
ārdrāyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ gaṅgāsnānaṃ sudurlabham //
2.40.d:
द्वादश्यां श्रवणर्क्षे च अष्टभ्यां पुष्ययोगतः ।
आर्द्रायां च चतुर्दश्यां गङ्गास्नानं सुदुर्लभम् ॥
2.40.m: On the twelfth [lunar day] with the Śravaṇā asterism, on the eighth with the Puṣya conjunction, / and on the fourteenth with Ārdrā, bathing in the Gaṅgā is very difficult to obtain.

2.40.s:
pūrṇimā mādhave puṇyā tathā kārtikamāghayoḥ /
amāvasyāstathaiteṣāṃ gaṅgāsnāne sudurlabhāḥ //
2.40.d:
पूर्णिमा माधवे पुण्या तथा कार्तिकमाघयोः ।
अमावस्यास्तथैतेषां गङ्गास्नाने सुदुर्लभाः ॥
2.40.m: The full moon in Mādhava is meritorious, as are those in Kārtika and Māgha; / likewise, the new moons of these [months] are very rare for bathing in the Gaṅgā.

2.40.s:
kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ sahasraṃ tu śataṃ syātsarvaparvasu /
amāyāṃ ca tathāṣṭamyāṃ māghāsitadale sati //
2.40.d:
कृष्णाष्टम्यां सहस्रं तु शतं स्यात्सर्वपर्वसु ।
अमायां च तथाष्टम्यां माघासितदले सति ॥
2.40.m: On the eighth of the dark fortnight, it is a thousandfold, but a hundredfold on all junction-days; / and when the eighth coincides with the new moon in the dark fortnight of Māgha,

2.40.s:
ardhodayaṃ tadā parvakiñcinnyūnaṃ mahodayaḥ /
mahodaye śataguṇaṃ lakṣamarddhodaye smṛtam //
2.40.d:
अर्धोदयं तदा पर्वकिञ्चिन्न्यूनं महोदयः ।
महोदये शतगुणं लक्षमर्द्धोदये स्मृतम् ॥
2.40.m: the junction is then called the 'half-rising' (ardhodaya); the 'great rising' (mahodaya) is slightly less [rare]. / In the mahodaya it is remembered as hundredfold, and in the ardhodaya a hundred thousandfold.

2.40.s:
snānaṃ gaṅgājale devi grahaṇāccandrasūryayoḥ /
māsatrayasnānaphalaṃ phālgunāṣāḍha māsayoḥ //
2.40.d:
स्नानं गङ्गाजले देवि ग्रहणाच्चन्द्रसूर्ययोः ।
मासत्रयस्नानफलं फाल्गुनाषाढ मासयोः ॥
2.40.m: O goddess, bathing in the Gaṅgā's water during an eclipse of the moon or sun / yields the fruit of three months' bathing in the months of Phālguna and Āṣāḍha.

2.40.s:
janmarkṣe tu kṛte snāne gaṅgāyāṃ bhaktibhāvataḥ /
janmaprabhṛti pāpaṃ vai saṃcitaṃ hi vinaśyati //
2.40.d:
जन्मर्क्षे तु कृते स्नाने गङ्गायां भक्तिभावतः ।
जन्मप्रभृति पापं वै संचितं हि विनश्यति ॥
2.40.m: When a bath is performed in the Gaṅgā with devotion on one's birth-asterism, / the sin accumulated from birth onward is indeed destroyed.

2.40.s:
caturdaśyāṃ māghakṛṣṇe vyatīpātaśca durlabhaḥ /
kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ viśeṣeṇa vaidhṛtirjāhnavījale //
2.40.d:
चतुर्दश्यां माघकृष्णे व्यतीपातश्च दुर्लभः ।
कृष्णाष्टम्यां विशेषेण वैधृतिर्जाह्नवीजले ॥
2.40.m: A Vyatīpāta on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight of Māgha is rare, / and especially a Vaidhṛti on the dark eighth in the waters of the Jāhnavī.

2.40.s:
māghaṃ sakalamevāpi naro yo vidhipūrvakam /
aruṇodayake snāyī sa tu jātismaro bhavet //
2.40.d:
माघं सकलमेवापि नरो यो विधिपूर्वकम् ।
अरुणोदयके स्नायी स तु जातिस्मरो भवेत् ॥
2.40.m: The man who bathes according to rule throughout the entire month of Māgha / at dawn becomes one who remembers his previous births.

2.40.s:
sarvaśāstrārthavijjñānī nīrogaśca bhavedbhruvam /
saṃkrāntyāṃ pakṣayorante grahaṇe candrasūryayoḥ //
2.40.d:
सर्वशास्त्रार्थविज्ज्ञानी नीरोगश्च भवेद्भ्रुवम् ।
संक्रान्त्यां पक्षयोरन्ते ग्रहणे चन्द्रसूर्ययोः ॥
2.40.m: He certainly becomes one who understands the meaning of all scriptures, wise, and free from disease. / On a transit, at the end of fortnights, and during an eclipse of the moon or sun,

2.40.s:
gaṅgāsnāto naraḥ kāmādbrahmaṇaḥ sadanaṃ labhet /
indorlakṣaguṇaṃ proktaṃ raverdaśaguṇaṃ tataḥ //
2.40.d:
गङ्गास्नातो नरः कामाद्ब्रह्मणः सदनं लभेत् ।
इन्दोर्लक्षगुणं प्रोक्तं रवेर्दशगुणं ततः ॥
2.40.m: a man bathed in the Gaṅgā attains Brahmā's abode as desired. / [The fruit] is said to be a hundred thousand times for the moon, and ten times that for the sun;

2.40.s:
gaṅgātīre tu saṃprāptā indoḥ koṭī raverdaśa /
vāruṇena samāyuktā madhau kṛṣṇā trayodaśī /
gaṅgāyāṃ yadi labhyeta sūryagrahaśataiḥ samā //
2.40.d:
गङ्गातीरे तु संप्राप्ता इन्दोः कोटी रवेर्दश ।
वारुणेन समायुक्ता मधौ कृष्णा त्रयोदशी ।
गङ्गायां यदि लभ्येत सूर्यग्रहशतैः समा ॥
2.40.m: reaching the bank of the Gaṅgā, it is ten million for the moon and a hundred million for the sun. / If the thirteenth of the dark fortnight in Madhu, joined with the Vāruṇa asterism, / is attained at the Gaṅgā, it is equal to hundreds of solar eclipses.

2.40.s:
jyeṣṭhe māsi kṣitisutadine śuklapakṣe daśamyāṃ haste śailādavataradasau jāhnavī martyalokam /
pāpānyasyāṃ harati hi tithau sā daśaiṣādyagaṅgā puṇyaṃ dadyādapi śataguṇaṃ vājimedhakratośca //
2.40.d:
ज्येष्ठे मासि क्षितिसुतदिने शुक्लपक्षे दशम्यां हस्ते शैलादवतरदसौ जाह्नवी मर्त्यलोकम् ।
पापान्यस्यां हरति हि तिथौ सा दशैषाद्यगङ्गा पुण्यं दद्यादपि शतगुणं वाजिमेधक्रतोश्च ॥
2.40.m: In the month of Jyeṣṭha, on Mars's day, in the bright fortnight, on the tenth, under Hasta, this Jāhnavī descended from the mountain to the mortal world; / on this lunar day, this primeval Gaṅgā takes away ten sins, and grants merit a hundred times that of a horse sacrifice.

2.40.s:
mahāpātakasaṃghāni yāni pāpāni saṃti me /
govindadvādaśīṃ prāpya tāni me hana jāhnavi //
2.40.d:
महापातकसंघानि यानि पापानि संति मे ।
गोविन्दद्वादशीं प्राप्य तानि मे हन जाह्नवि ॥
2.40.m: [Reciting:] 'Whatever sins I have that constitute masses of great sins, / having reached Govindadvādaśī, destroy them for me, O Jāhnavī!'

2.40.s:
maghāsaṃjñena ṛkṣeṇa candraḥ saṃpūrṇamaṇḍalaḥ /
guruṇā yāti saṃyogaṃ tanmahatvaṃ titheḥ smṛtam //
2.40.d:
मघासंज्ञेन ऋक्षेण चन्द्रः संपूर्णमण्डलः ।
गुरुणा याति संयोगं तन्महत्वं तिथेः स्मृतम् ॥
2.40.m: When the full disc of the moon, in the asterism named Maghā, / enters conjunction with Jupiter, that greatness of the lunar day is remembered.

2.40.s:
gaṅgāyāṃ yadi labhyeta sūryagrahaśataiḥ samā /
atha deśaviśeṣeṇa snānasya phalamucyate //
2.40.d:
गङ्गायां यदि लभ्येत सूर्यग्रहशतैः समा ।
अथ देशविशेषेण स्नानस्य फलमुच्यते ॥
2.40.m: If attained at the Gaṅgā, it is equal to hundreds of solar eclipses. / Now the fruit of bathing according to specific places is stated.

2.40.s:
kurukṣetrāddaśaguṇā yatra tatrāvagāhitā /
kurukṣetrācchataguṇā yatra vindhyena saṃyutā //
2.40.d:
कुरुक्षेत्राद्दशगुणा यत्र तत्रावगाहिता ।
कुरुक्षेत्राच्छतगुणा यत्र विन्ध्येन संयुता ॥
2.40.m: Wherever one plunges into it, it is ten times greater than Kurukṣetra; / where it joins with the Vindhya, it is a hundred times greater than Kurukṣetra;

2.40.s:
vindhyācchataguṇā proktā kāśīpuryāṃ tu jāhnavī /
sarvatra durlabhā gaṅgā triṣu sthāneṣu cādhikā //
2.40.d:
विन्ध्याच्छतगुणा प्रोक्ता काशीपुर्यां तु जाह्नवी ।
सर्वत्र दुर्लभा गङ्गा त्रिषु स्थानेषु चाधिका ॥
2.40.m: in the city of Kāśī, the Jāhnavī is declared a hundred times greater than the Vindhya. / The Gaṅgā is everywhere difficult to attain, but in three places it is superior:

2.40.s:
gaṅgādvāre prayāge ca gaṅgāsāgarasaṃgame /
eṣu snātā divaṃ yānti ye mṛtāste 'punarbhavāḥ //
2.40.d:
गङ्गाद्वारे प्रयागे च गङ्गासागरसंगमे ।
एषु स्नाता दिवं यान्ति ये मृतास्ते ऽपुनर्भवाः ॥
2.40.m: at Gaṅgādvāra, at Prayāga, and at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean. / Those who bathe in these go to heaven; those who die there are free from rebirth.

2.40.s:
gaṅgādvāre kuśāvarte snāne puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu /
saptānāṃ rājasūyānāṃ phalaṃ syādaśvamedhayoḥ //
2.40.d:
गङ्गाद्वारे कुशावर्ते स्नाने पुण्यफलं शृणु ।
सप्तानां राजसूयानां फलं स्यादश्वमेधयोः ॥
2.40.m: Hear the meritorious fruit of bathing at Gaṅgādvāra and Kuśāvarta: / there is the fruit of seven Rājasūyas and of two horse sacrifices.

2.40.s:
uṣitvā tatra māsārddhaṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ viśvajitāṃ phalam /
daśāyutānāṃ tu gavāṃ dānapuṇyaṃ vidurbudhāḥ //
2.40.d:
उषित्वा तत्र मासार्द्धं षण्णां विश्वजितां फलम् ।
दशायुतानां तु गवां दानपुण्यं विदुर्बुधाः ॥
2.40.m: Residing there for half a month yields the fruit of six Viśvajit sacrifices; / the wise know the merit to be equal to the gift of a hundred thousand cows.

2.40.s:
sarottame 'tha govindaṃ rudraṃ kanakhale sthitam /
snātvā vāpyeṣu gaṅgāyāṃ puṇyamakṣayamāpnuyāt //
2.40.d:
सरोत्तमे ऽथ गोविन्दं रुद्रं कनखले स्थितम् ।
स्नात्वा वाप्येषु गङ्गायां पुण्यमक्षयमाप्नुयात् ॥
2.40.m: Then, having worshipped Govinda in the best lake, and Rudra situated at Kanakhala, / or having bathed in these along the Gaṅgā, one attains imperishable merit.

2.40.s:
tīrthaṃ ca saukaraṃ nāma mahāpuṇyaṃ śubhe śṛṇu /
yasminnāvirabhūtpūrvaṃ vārāhākṛtiracyutaḥ //
2.40.d:
तीर्थं च सौकरं नाम महापुण्यं शुभे शृणु ।
यस्मिन्नाविरभूत्पूर्वं वाराहाकृतिरच्युतः ॥
2.40.m: Hear, O auspicious one, of the highly meritorious sacred ford named Saukara, / where in ancient times Acyuta appeared in the form of a boar.

2.40.s:
śatasyāgnicitāṃ puṇyaṃ jyotiṣṭomadvayasya ca /
agniṣṭomasahasrasya phalamāpnoti mānavaḥ //
2.40.d:
शतस्याग्निचितां पुण्यं ज्योतिष्टोमद्वयस्य च ।
अग्निष्टोमसहस्रस्य फलमाप्नोति मानवः ॥
2.40.m: A human being obtains the merit of a hundred Agnicits, of two Jyotiṣṭomas, / and the fruit of a thousand Agniṣṭomas.

2.40.s:
tatraiva brahmaṇastīrthe jyotiṣṭomāyutasya ca /
aśvamedhatrayasyāpi snātaḥ puṇyaṃ labhennaraḥ //
2.40.d:
तत्रैव ब्रह्मणस्तीर्थे ज्योतिष्टोमायुतस्य च ।
अश्वमेधत्रयस्यापि स्नातः पुण्यं लभेन्नरः ॥
2.40.m: At that very place, in the sacred ford of Brahmā, a man who has bathed / obtains the merit of ten thousand Jyotiṣṭomas and of three horse sacrifices.

2.40.s:
kubjākhyaṃ tīrthamanaghaṃ yatra ca vyādhayo 'khilāḥ /
naśyanti sarvajanmotthaṃ pātakaṃ cāpi mohini //
2.40.d:
कुब्जाख्यं तीर्थमनघं यत्र च व्याधयो ऽखिलाः ।
नश्यन्ति सर्वजन्मोत्थं पातकं चापि मोहिनि ॥
2.40.m: The faultless sacred ford named Kubja, where all diseases / are destroyed, as well as sin arisen from all births, O Mohinī;

2.40.s:
atrānyatkāpilaṃ tīrthaṃ yatra snāto naraḥ śubhe /
kapilāṣṭāyutasyāpi dānatulyaphalaṃ labhet //
2.40.d:
अत्रान्यत्कापिलं तीर्थं यत्र स्नातो नरः शुभे ।
कपिलाष्टायुतस्यापि दानतुल्यफलं लभेत् ॥
2.40.m: here is another, the Kāpila sacred ford, bathing where, O auspicious one, / a man obtains the fruit equal to the gift of eighty thousand brown cows.

2.40.s:
gaṅgādvāre kuśāvarte bilvake nīlaparvate /
tīrthe kanakhale snātvā dhūtapāpo vrajeddivam //
2.40.d:
गङ्गाद्वारे कुशावर्ते बिल्वके नीलपर्वते ।
तीर्थे कनखले स्नात्वा धूतपापो व्रजेद्दिवम् ॥
2.40.m: At Gaṅgādvāra, Kuśāvarta, Bilvaka, the Nīla mountain, / and in the sacred ford at Kanakhala, having bathed and shaken off sin, one goes to heaven.

2.40.s:
pavitrārthaṃ tatastīrthaṃ sarvatīrthottamottamam /
dvayorviśvajitostatra snānātpuṇyaṃ labhennaraḥ //
2.40.d:
पवित्रार्थं ततस्तीर्थं सर्वतीर्थोत्तमोत्तमम् ।
द्वयोर्विश्वजितोस्तत्र स्नानात्पुण्यं लभेन्नरः ॥
2.40.m: Then there is the sacred ford for purification, the highest of all the best sacred fords; / bathing there, a man obtains the merit of two Viśvajit sacrifices.

2.40.s:
veṇīrājyaṃ tatastīrthaṃ sarayūryatra gaṅgayā /
supuṇyayā mahāpuṇyā svasā svasreva saṃgatā //
2.40.d:
वेणीराज्यं ततस्तीर्थं सरयूर्यत्र गङ्गया ।
सुपुण्यया महापुण्या स्वसा स्वस्रेव संगता ॥
2.40.m: Then there is the sacred ford Veṇīrājya, where the Sarayū meets the Gaṅgā, / the highly meritorious meeting the very meritorious, like a sister meeting a sister.

2.40.s:
harerdakṣiṇapādābjakṣālanādamarāpagā /
vāmapādodbhavā vāpi sarayūrmānasaprasūḥ //
2.40.d:
हरेर्दक्षिणपादाब्जक्षालनादमरापगा ।
वामपादोद्भवा वापि सरयूर्मानसप्रसूः ॥
2.40.m: From the washing of Hari's right lotus-foot came the river of the immortals, / and from the left foot arose the Sarayū, whose source is Mānasa.

2.40.s:
tīrthe tatrārcayan rudraṃ viṣṇuṃ viṣṇutvamāpnuyāt /
pañcāśvamedhaphaladaṃ snānaṃ tatra prakīrtitam //
2.40.d:
तीर्थे तत्रार्चयन् रुद्रं विष्णुं विष्णुत्वमाप्नुयात् ।
पञ्चाश्वमेधफलदं स्नानं तत्र प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
2.40.m: Worshipping Rudra and Viṣṇu in that sacred ford, one attains the state of Viṣṇu; / bathing there is proclaimed to give the fruit of five horse sacrifices.

2.40.s:
tatastu gāṇḍavaṃ tīrthaṃ gaṇḍakī yatra saṃgatā /
gosahasrasya dānaṃ ca tatra snānaṃ samaṃ dvayam //
2.40.d:
ततस्तु गाण्डवं तीर्थं गण्डकी यत्र संगता ।
गोसहस्रस्य दानं च तत्र स्नानं समं द्वयम् ॥
2.40.m: Then there is the Gāṇḍava sacred ford, where the Gaṇḍakī unites [with it]; / the gift of a thousand cows and bathing there—the two are equal.

2.40.s:
rāmatīrthaṃ tataḥ puṇyaṃ vaikuṇṭhaṃ yatra sannidhau /
somatīrthaṃ tataḥ puṇyaṃ yatrāsau nakulo muniḥ //
2.40.d:
रामतीर्थं ततः पुण्यं वैकुण्ठं यत्र सन्निधौ ।
सोमतीर्थं ततः पुण्यं यत्रासौ नकुलो मुनिः ॥
2.40.m: Then there is the meritorious Rāmatīrtha, in whose vicinity is Vaikuṇṭha; / then the meritorious Somatīrtha, where the sage Nakula,

2.40.s:
samabhyarcya śivaṃ dhyāyangaṇatāṃ tu samāyayau /
caṃpakākhyaṃ puṇyatīrthaṃ yadgaṅgottaravāhinī //
2.40.d:
समभ्यर्च्य शिवं ध्यायन्गणतां तु समाययौ ।
चंपकाख्यं पुण्यतीर्थं यद्गङ्गोत्तरवाहिनी ॥
2.40.m: having worshipped Śiva while meditating, attained the status of an attendant. / The meritorious sacred ford named Campaka is where the Gaṅgā flows northward;

2.40.s:
maṇikarṇikayā tulyaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam /
kalaśākhyaṃ tatastīrthaṃ kalaśādutthito muniḥ //
2.40.d:
मणिकर्णिकया तुल्यं महापातकनाशनम् ।
कलशाख्यं ततस्तीर्थं कलशादुत्थितो मुनिः ॥
2.40.m: equal to Maṇikarṇikā, it destroys great sins. / Then there is the sacred ford named Kalaśa, where the sage born from a jar,

2.40.s:
agastyaḥ pūjayanyatra rudraṃ munivaro 'bhavat /
somadvīpaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ tīrthaṃ vārāṇasīsamam //
2.40.d:
अगस्त्यः पूजयन्यत्र रुद्रं मुनिवरो ऽभवत् ।
सोमद्वीपं महापुण्यं तीर्थं वाराणसीसमम् ॥
2.40.m: Agastya, worshipping Rudra, became the best of sages. / Somadvīpa is a highly meritorious sacred ford equal to Vārāṇasī,

2.40.s:
somo yatrārcayannīśaṃ rudreṇa śirasā dhṛtaḥ /
viśvāmitrasya bhaginī gaṅgayā yatra saṃgatā //
2.40.d:
सोमो यत्रार्चयन्नीशं रुद्रेण शिरसा धृतः ।
विश्वामित्रस्य भगिनी गङ्गया यत्र संगता ॥
2.40.m: where Soma, worshipping the Lord, was held by Rudra on his head. / Where the sister of Viśvāmitra meets with the Gaṅgā,

2.40.s:
tatrāpluto naro bhūyādvāsavasya priyo 'tithiḥ /
jahnuhrade mahātīrthe snāto martyo hi mohini //
2.40.d:
तत्राप्लुतो नरो भूयाद्वासवस्य प्रियो ऽतिथिः ।
जह्नुह्रदे महातीर्थे स्नातो मर्त्यो हि मोहिनि ॥
2.40.m: a man bathed there becomes a dear guest of Vāsava. / When a mortal bathes in the great sacred ford Jahnuhrada, O Mohinī,

2.40.s:
ekaviṃśatikulyānāṃ tārako bhavati dhruvam /
tasmādadititīrthaṃ ca yatrāvāpāditirharim //
2.40.d:
एकविंशतिकुल्यानां तारको भवति ध्रुवम् ।
तस्माददितितीर्थं च यत्रावापादितिर्हरिम् ॥
2.40.m: he certainly becomes the saviour of twenty-one generations. / Thence there is the Adititīrtha, where Aditi obtained Hari

2.40.s:
kaśyapāttatra subhage snānamāhurmahodayam /
śiloccayaṃ mahātīrthaṃ yatra taptvā tapaḥ prajāḥ //
2.40.d:
कश्यपात्तत्र सुभगे स्नानमाहुर्महोदयम् ।
शिलोच्चयं महातीर्थं यत्र तप्त्वा तपः प्रजाः ॥
2.40.m: from Kaśyapa; bathing there, O fortunate one, is said to bring great rising. / Śiloccaya is a great sacred ford where, having performed austerities, the creatures

2.40.s:
tṛṇādibhiḥ saha svargaṃ yānti tīrthagaṇāśrayāt /
indrāṇīnāmatīrthaṃ syādyatrendrāṇī tu vāsavam //
2.40.d:
तृणादिभिः सह स्वर्गं यान्ति तीर्थगणाश्रयात् ।
इन्द्राणीनामतीर्थं स्याद्यत्रेन्द्राणी तु वासवम् ॥
2.40.m: go to heaven together with grass and other things, through taking refuge in the host of sacred fords. / There is the sacred ford named Indrāṇī, where Indrāṇī indeed, [having performed austerities],

2.40.s:
tapastaptvā patiṃ lebhe sevyametatprayāgavat /
puṇyadaṃ snātakaṃ tīrthaṃ viśvāmitrastapaścaran //
2.40.d:
तपस्तप्त्वा पतिं लेभे सेव्यमेतत्प्रयागवत् ।
पुण्यदं स्नातकं तीर्थं विश्वामित्रस्तपश्चरन् ॥
2.40.m: obtained Vāsava as her husband; this is to be resorted to like Prayāga. / There is the merit-yielding sacred ford Snātaka, where Viśvāmitra, practicing austerities,

2.40.s:
yatra brahmarṣitāṃ lebhe kṣattriyastīrthā sevayā /
pradyumnatīrthaṃ tapasā khyātaṃ yatra smaro hareḥ //
2.40.d:
यत्र ब्रह्मर्षितां लेभे क्षत्त्रियस्तीर्था सेवया ।
प्रद्युम्नतीर्थं तपसा ख्यातं यत्र स्मरो हरेः ॥
2.40.m: attained the status of a brahmin sage though a kṣatriya, through service to the sacred ford. / Pradyumnatīrtha is renowned through penance, where the god of love [became] Hari's

2.40.s:
pradyumnanāmā putro 'bhūtparaṃ tatra mahodayam /
tato dakṣaprayāgaṃ tu gaṅgāto yamunāgata //
2.40.d:
प्रद्युम्ननामा पुत्रो ऽभूत्परं तत्र महोदयम् ।
ततो दक्षप्रयागं तु गङ्गातो यमुनागत ॥
2.40.m: son named Pradyumna; there is supreme prosperity there. / Then, to Dakṣaprayāga, going from the Gaṅgā to the Yamunā,

2.40.s:
snātvā tatrākṣayaṃ puṇyaṃ prayāga iva labhyate //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇottarabhāge mohinīvasusaṃvāde gaṅgāmāhātmye sthalaviśeṣasnānaphalakathanaṃ nāma catvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.40.d:
स्नात्वा तत्राक्षयं पुण्यं प्रयाग इव लभ्यते ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणोत्तरभागे मोहिनीवसुसंवादे गङ्गामाहात्म्ये स्थलविशेषस्नानफलकथनं नाम चत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
2.40.m:
bathing there, imperishable merit is obtained just as at Prayāga.

Thus ends the fortieth chapter, entitled "The Declaration of the Fruits of Bathing at Particular Places" in the Eulogy of the Greatness of the Gaṅgā, in the conversation between Mohinī and Vasu in the latter part of the illustrious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.
